#3282. Did the AI bubble just pop? $2 trillion reality check hits Nvidia, Meta & SpaceX as Wall Street panics, signaling a potential end to RAM crisis in 2027

If you want to know what it looks like when a trillion-dollar tech bubble violently collides with physical reality, just look at yesterday. $2.5 trillion in tech valuations were wiped off the board as Wall Street panicked about AI’s leverage — punishing tech giants for incinerating cash on infrastructure that isn’t generating immediate profit.

Simultaneously, as we saw on Wednesday, the American voter rejected data center expansions in 40 out of 41 local ballot measures. The hardware hoarders are losing their grip, and the panic is palpable. The era of scrutiny is here, and I want to show you two possible timelines of where this could go.

But first, we have to go back over a couple things.

When faced with this stock crash, AMD CEO Lisa Su said, “We are a data center first company.” While I’d love to throw my hands up and get angry at this, I have to turn the BS detector on myself and address a brutal truth: she’s right. This market crash is a sentiment correction, not an overnight fab cancellation.

The big three memory foundries — SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron — operate on long-term agreements. 2026-2027 is already locked in at sky-high prices, and on top of that, enterprise AI accelerators consume roughly 3x the silicon wafers of standard consumer DDR5 memory.

As long as those massive AI server chips are shipping, conventional RAM capacity remains deeply suppressed.

So, if Wall Street is slashing valuations and data center permits are being blocked, why aren’t memory foundries pivoting back to consumer PC hardware right now?

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

Hyperscalers are also starving for memory, and receive around 60-70% of what they ask for. If Microsoft and Meta get spooked by the market and pull back their massive order growth by 10% or even 15%, it wouldn’t trigger a supply chain pivot. It just means the foundries are a little less overwhelmed. Demand still vastly exceeds total factory capacity.

If foundries are still frantically trying to fulfill enterprise contracts, they have zero financial incentive to redirect back to consumer memory.

For them to actually panic and pivot, hyperscaler orders have to crater. A simple market correction like this won’t do it. But a sweeping wave of municipal zoning bans? That changes the math entirely.

Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence.November 4, 2026

If tech giants are legally barred from breaking ground on new server farms, they are forced to cancel their existing silicon orders because they physically have nowhere to plug the chips in.

We are not getting a massive surplus of GPUs and memory kits tomorrow morning. But the midterms and the stock market correction did put a concrete ceiling on the shortage. So let me take a stab at how I think this is going to unfold.

The stock rout has cracked the leveraged AI market for now, but contract prices remain firm. There is zero immediate relief, so don’t expect some banger Black Friday deals on RTX 5090s.

Memory shortages will hit their tightest consumer squeeze through early 2027. PC makers will fiercely defend a ceiling of 16GB-24GB on premium laptops and handhelds. If you’re hoping for 32GB in sub-$1,500 machines, shelve that hope through most of next year.

As hyperscalers face sustained stock and regulatory pressure from the midterm fallout, corporate boards will force company CFOs to look at their data center infrastructure plans again.

Instead of writing blank checks for server racks, the pace of subsequent purchase orders will slow. And for you reading this, I envision that PC hardware prices will finally stop climbing and plateau.

PC builders (Apple, Dell, Asus, Lenovo, etc) will gain massive leverage during mid-year procurement negotiations — putting an end to double-digit quarter-on-quarter price hikes.

A typical memory wafer run takes 3-4 months. Once the AI server orders officially ease in Q2, foundries will finally redirect their wafers back to consumer products. This is when the true price relief begins.

Standard desktop DDR5 kits will experience price drops, and holiday 2027 laptops will finally start normalizing 32GB unified configurations without severe margin penalties.

We aren’t completely out of the woods, and we still have to survive a brutal winter. But in my mind, those 2028 doom-and-gloom shortage predictions are officially dead.

The hyperscalers just hit a political and financial ceiling, which may lead to a peak in memory pricing this spring rather than running unchecked into next year.

Hold off on your PC upgrades — the local AI renaissance could be scheduled for the second half of 2027.

#3281. It’s Possible You’ve Been Making Coffee All Wrong: 6 Mistakes a Pro Says to Avoid

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Avoid these brewing blunders for coffee that tastes like the stuff baristas make.

I make coffee every morning, almost without fail. I haven’t always used the same method, and because I bounce between processes to test and experiment with coffee makers, beans and, yes, even K-Cups, I’m open to the idea that I might not always get it right.

According to Sarina Prabasi, the founder of Buunni micro-roastery in New York City, I’m in good company.

Prabasi serves on the board of the Specialty Coffee Association and assures me I’m probably making one or two common coffee-brewing mistakes, like everyone else. Coffee is nuanced; it’s easy to fall into habits—often passed down from family, and often bad.

Whether you brew your morning coffee with a pour-over, French press or espresso machine, here are six coffee mistakes to avoid.

Even the slightest film of soap residue can taint your next cup.

Ditching the soap for your coffee pot and pour-over immersion brewer might seem like dubious advice. In reality, your coffee equipment doesn’t need a scrub down every time you use it. Even small amounts of residue from fragrant dish soap detergent will leave you with a sudsy, subpar pot of coffee.

“It really stays in there; it can mess with the flavor, and so, usually, a good rinse with super hot water is enough for black coffee,” Prabasi said. Oils from the beans may build up over time, so fragrance-free dish soap comes in handy for occasional deep cleaning. A simple rinse with hot water will more than suffice for daily use, however. Save yourself time and avoid any unwanted “soap scum” notes that might interrupt the notes of your single-origin Sidama natural roast.

Coffee beans are one pantry staple you shouldn’t buy in bulk.

Buying in bulk can save time and money at the grocery store, but it can disappoint coffee drinkers. Buying smaller quantities of beans helps you avoid stale, flat coffee, especially for average drinkers and households with one or two people. Probasi told us that you’ll know coffee has gone stale because it “can taste like a shadow of itself.”

The roaster recommends checking the coffee label for a roast date within one month, ideally within two weeks. (Keep in mind, the “best buy” date is different and isn’t an indicator of freshness.) If you don’t like grinding at home, the roast date should be on the fresher side.

But you needn’t panic about the declining flavor in your cupboard like a ticking time bomb. “Every day post-roast doesn’t mean it’s losing freshness, but after two weeks, I’d say it starts to go down,” Prabasi said. Store coffee in an airtight container but avoid the humid fridge with its plethora of smells that can stick to the beans.

You can find tutorials online recommending brewers, scales, tampers, water filters, grinders and miscellaneous techniques to make the perfect cup. Experimentation is key to crafting your favorite brew but only if you start with the basics. “So just adjust only the water in the beginning,” Prabasi said.

If you don’t have a kitchen scale, the roaster told us the rule of thumb is to start with two tablespoons of ground coffee per cup of water. The finer the grind, the stronger your coffee will taste, so adjust the grounds-to-water ratio accordingly. If that seems too weak or too strong, then adjust by adding more or less coffee at the same grind level.

Beyond the basics, you can get creative. “If your coffee is too sour, it’s maybe that you prefer a dark roast,” Prabasi said. Coffee too bitter? You can adjust the roast type by buying a level down, such as dark to medium or medium to light. “ If you got a coffee from East Africa, maybe try one from South America, you know, like switch [it] around,” she said. Changing one element at a time ensures you know which step affected the result, for better or worse.

Filling your coffee pot with tap water will yield less-than-ideal flavors. For most of us, filtered water will make a big difference in your coffee’s final flavor. Tap water often contains by-products that a home water filtration system can easily remove.

Almost all tap water in the US is disinfected with low levels of chlorine. This chemical helps keep drinking water safe as it leaves treatment centers but can alter the taste and smell of tap water. Chloramines can also strip lead and copper from pipes, by-products that can affect even the most carefully prepared coffee.

Smell can be a dead giveaway that your coffee has gone stale. Prabasi explains that you should immediately open a bag of beans or ground coffee and smell the roasted coffee scent. Aroma is a key indicator of flavor. No aroma means a serious lack of taste.

Prabasi said stale coffee can taste muddy or flat and lack any complex tasting notes that a bag might list on its label. “ That’s why I think for in the coffee profession, so much of what we do is tasting coffee,” she said. “From the farm to the coffee shop, every step of the way coffee gets tasted or cupped, in our vernacular.”

Old coffee isn’t likely to make you sick, so there’s no need to toss it. You might, however, want to shift from taking your coffee black. Making iced coffee is a simple way to mask the lack of tasting notes. An immersion brewer also lets you steep the grounds longer to add a bit more flavor after the coffee has dulled.

Don’t skimp on organic coffee even if it costs a few bucks more.

The multitude of coffee brands at the grocery store can feel overwhelming. To help sift through the masses, Prabasi explains the organic coffee label is a sign of quality that’s important for coffee.

“If you can, then I think for coffee and tea, organic is really important because coffee and tea crops, especially from large farms, tend to get really over-sprayed,” Prabasi said. Pesticides are sprayed right onto the coffee cherries, and coffee is unlike an apple that you can wash or a banana that you peel before eating. Tea leaves go through a similar process, and anything left on the leaves then steeps into your mug.

The coffeehouse owner made it clear that she doesn’t believe coffee needs to be expensive to be considered “good.” Great coffee comes in a variety of price points. ” I think the care that goes into sourcing it, to roasting it, or just serving it, I would be looking for those things,” Prabasi said. The organic label is a helpful place to start.

#3280. Dell vs. Nvidia: Chip Stocks Just Suffered Their Worst Sell-Off Since 2020. Which Is the Better Buy for 2027?

Dell's cash flow and NVIDIA's margins tell very different stories, and a sizable valuation gap may matter more than either name suggests.

The artificial intelligence (AI) boom has fueled extraordinary growth across the technology sector, but a recent sell-off has Wall Street questioning whether massive infrastructure investments can continue to justify elevated valuations. For investors looking toward 2027, the pullback presents an opportunity to reassess two major beneficiaries of the AI boom: Dell Technologies(DELL +3.67%) and Nvidia (NVDA +2.77%).

Dell provides the servers and infrastructure needed to support AI workloads, while Nvidia designs the advanced chips powering them. Both have benefited from surging demand, but their business models, profitability, and valuations differ substantially. As investors become more selective about AI exposure, those differences could determine which stock offers the more compelling long-term opportunity.

Dell provides servers, storage systems, and personal computers to enterprises, governments, and cloud providers. Its Infrastructure Solutions Group has become an increasingly important driver of growth as demand for AI-optimized servers accelerates.

In fiscal 2026, Dell generated $113.5 billion in revenue, an increase of approximately 19% year over year. Net income reached $5.9 billion, representing a profit margin of 5.2%. More recent results highlight the momentum behind its AI business. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue surged 58% to $47 billion, with AI-optimized server revenue doubling to $16.4 billion. Dell also reported a $95 billion AI server backlog, providing considerable visibility into future demand, although orders remain subject to customer spending decisions.

At the end of fiscal 2026, its debt-to-equity ratio was negative due to a shareholder equity deficit, while its current ratio stood near 0.9x. Nevertheless, the company generated substantial operating cash flow, providing resources to fund operations and return capital to shareholders.

NVIDIA is a leader in semiconductor stocks, supplying the GPUs, networking equipment, and software infrastructure powering much of the industry's expansion.

In fiscal 2026, Nvidia generated $215.9 billion in revenue, an increase of approximately 65% year over year. Net income reached $120.1 billion, representing an exceptional profit margin of 55.6%. More recent results highlight continued momentum. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue surged 106% to $96.2 billion, driven by a 117% increase in data center revenue to $89 billion.

Nvidia also maintains an exceptionally strong financial position. At the end of fiscal 2026, its debt-to-equity ratio stood near 0.1x, while its current ratio was approximately 3.9x. The company generated roughly $96.6 billion in free cash flow during the year, providing substantial financial flexibility to invest in new technologies.

Dell faces intense competition from rivals like Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE +1.38%), particularly in the rapidly expanding AI server market. Its relatively thin profit margins leave less room for rising costs or pricing pressure, while reliance on a concentrated group of large AI customers creates additional risk if infrastructure spending slows.

Nvidia faces a different set of challenges. Its dominant position in AI computing is increasingly being challenged by AMD (AMD +11.04%) and custom chips developed by major cloud providers. Heavy reliance on a relatively small number of customers exposes the company to changes in their capital spending plans, while dependence on Asian manufacturers introduces geopolitical and supply chain risks.

Both companies remain vulnerable to a slowdown in AI infrastructure investment. However, Dell faces greater margin and balance-sheet pressures, while Nvidia must defend its market leadership and justify the substantial growth expectations surrounding its business.

Dell appears more attractively priced for value-conscious investors based on its lower Forward P/E and P/S ratio than its rival.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

The recent sell-off across AI and technology stocks has raised legitimate questions about the sustainability of massive infrastructure spending. However, the latest earnings from Dell and Nvidia suggest that demand remains strong, even as investors grow increasingly cautious about valuations and future growth expectations.From a valuation standpoint, Dell appears significantly cheaper. It trades at 14.2 times forward earnings and 1.5 times sales, compared with Nvidia at 21.7 times forward earnings and 16.1 times sales. Dell's lower valuation could offer substantial upside if AI infrastructure spending remains elevated, although its relatively thin profit margins and balance-sheet constraints introduce additional risks.Nvidia's premium valuation, however, reflects a fundamentally different business. Its dominant position in AI computing, exceptional profitability, and substantial free cash flow provide financial strength that Dell cannot match. With a net profit margin exceeding 55%, Nvidia captures considerably more value from the AI boom, while its software ecosystem and technological leadership provide competitive advantages that could support continued growth.For investors looking toward 2027, Nvidia is the better buy. The recent correction has made valuations increasingly important, but Nvidia's combination of earnings growth, financial strength, and market leadership offers a more compelling investment case.

#3279. iOS 27.3: New features, release date, more

This week, Apple released the first iOS 27.3 beta. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left to make it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

#3278. Roku is taking away a fan-favorite screensaver – but you have alternatives

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

One of Roku's most popular screensavers is about to make its last splash. Here’s how to switch before Dec. 1.

A fan-favorite Roku screensaver is going away, and users aren’t happy.

Over the last several days, users with the Aquatic Life aquarium screensaver set as the default have noticed a message appearing when the screensaver opens. “Starting Dec. 1, 2026,” the message reads, “the Aquatic Life screensaver will no longer be available, and your screensaver will switch to Roku City.”

Also: The free Roku City screensaver game has me hooked

The screensaver, which displays a digital aquarium with tropical fish swimming back and forth, was available as a downloadable theme pack and was a popular pick for many years.

Users on Reddit quickly lamented the loss in many posts, with dozens noting that the aquarium was part of their daily routine. Roku responded to one post, saying, “That makes sense, and we hear you. Aquatic Life has a lot of loyal fans, and we’re passing your feedback along to the team.” The post noted that when “the fish swim off,” Roku devices with Aquatic Life will switch to Roku City.

You can browse to Settings > Theme > Screensaver to find another theme.

Several online reports indicate that the removal is a licensing issue and that the creator of the screensaver posted on Reddit that he removed the license after Roku’s sale to Fox. That thread has now been deleted, so the comment is unavailable. Roku hasn’t issued any statement of its own about why, but I have reached out to ask. I’ve also reached out directly to the screensaver’s creator.

If you’re looking for the exact screensaver, it’s still available as a 2-minute clip on Roku’s YouTube channel. It takes a few extra steps, but if you want to keep the screensaver running on your TV, you can create a YouTube playlist with just that video, set it to loop, and use the YouTube app on Roku whenever you want to see it.

Even though the announcement of the screensaver’s departure happened less than 24 hours ago, the comments section of that video is packed with users begging Roku to keep Aquatic Life.

Also: I started clearing my Roku cache, and it fixed my biggest TV complaint

Alternatively, you could open one of the many YouTube videos that have aquarium displays and let one of them run for as long as you want.

There are also several dozen aquarium apps for Roku. I checked out several of them, and while they don’t look exactly like the Roku one, they do fill the void. Note that if you opt for one of these, most of them do have ads that play before the aquarium starts.

Lastly, you can download the original app for your phone or computer from SereneScreen.

#3276. The Clock Is Running on Apple’s Siri Settlement. How to File Before Dec. 21

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or iPhone 16 model between June 2024 and March 2025 is eligible to file a claim.

Dec. 21 is the last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features, and payouts could reach $95 per eligible iPhone.

The class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet. Filing takes a few minutes online, and each qualifying phone gets its own claim.

The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing. However, the first AI features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, several weeks later, and the most heavily promoted one, a Siri that could pull personal context from your apps, was further delayed in March 2025.

Now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website. The opt-in form is available only for a limited time, so get your name in the pool before it closes. Eligible buyers have until Dec. 21 to file, and each qualifying iPhone gets its own claim.

Apple settled a false advertising lawsuit brought by Clarkson Law Firm in May, agreeing to pay $250 million to customers who bought some iPhone models during a specified period. The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled customers by promising AI features that didn’t ship with the new devices. Apple denies all of the lawsuit’s allegations and denies that it did anything unlawful or improper.

If you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement. Payouts between $25 and $95 per eligible device are expected.

“Apple has reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features. We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our users,” an Apple spokesperson said in an earlier statement to CNET.

The court granted preliminary approval of the settlement on July 17. Then an Aug. 13 order moved up the final approval date by seven months.

“False advertising settlements aim to raise the floor of truth-telling, protect fair competition and increase consumer choice,” said Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, in a statement to CNET. He claimed it’s the largest false-advertising settlement in history.

Apple lit up its flagship New York City store to resemble Siri’s new color scheme.

As of Sept. 21, you can go to SmartphoneAISettlement.com and enter your information to confirm your eligibility for monetary relief. People whom Apple and the settlement administrator determined would be eligible will also receive email or postal notices from the company Verita directing them to the website.

The claims window closes on Dec. 21, 2026, so you have three months to act.

If you bought one of the following devices between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you could be eligible to receive a settlement payment:

The iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max are included because they have the processor and memory to run Apple Intelligence features.

It’s estimated that approximately 36 million customers are eligible for this settlement.

When Apple advertised its new iPhone 16 lineup in 2024, it emphasized how the models were optimized for AI features such as an enhanced Siri that could act as an intelligent agent. When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.

According to the proposed settlement, “Apple allegedly saturated the market with deceptive ads, inducing consumers to purchase iPhones based on the promise of certain enhanced Siri features.”

Some features of Apple Intelligence did ship soon after the introduction of the iPhone 16 and iOS 18, including Visual Intelligence, Live Translation, Writing Tools, Genmoji and Clean Up. But those weren’t the advanced features Apple highlighted. In fact, the type of intelligent interactions Apple advertised is only starting to show up in Siri AI, which is part of iOS 27, which was released in early September.

According to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval. As of late July, preliminary approval has been granted by the court.

After the data is provided and verified, a 45-day notice period begins to inform potential consumers that they’re eligible for a payment.

On Aug. 13, US District Court Judge Noël Wise granted approval to push forward the date from Sept. 29, 2027, to Feb. 24, 2027.

Provided approval is granted, the first checks or deposits will arrive sometime within a 60-day window after February next year, depending on court dates and possible extensions.

#3275. SK Hynix Just Announced Huge News for Micron Shareholders

SK Hynix's long-term outlook should have Micron investors excited.

Korean memory chip company SK Hynix (SKHY +2.78%) is one of the major players in this industry and a competitor to Micron Technology (MU +5.12%). So, how can its announcement of huge news affect Micron? Well, it has to deal with the state of the industry that these two operate in.

There isn't a ton that separates one memory chip producer from another, and the products are fairly commoditized. As a result, chip prices are highly driven by supply and demand laws.

Right now, demand is high, and supply is low, so prices are soaring. While times are good right now, the market is worried that demand will eventually soften, and the companies in this space will see their businesses collapse as a result. However, SK Hynix just pushed that date out further.

During its most recent earnings report, SK Hynix noted that its DRAM and HBM (high bandwidth memory, the type that's utilized in AI computing units) were sold out through 2029. That's big news, and most likely the same will happen to Micron as well.

As a result, demand for memory chips will remain high, which should boost Micron's stock. The market hasn't priced this in yet, so now is the perfect time to buy.

Micron has been vocal about market conditions, but that hasn't been reflected in the company's stock price. Micron told investors during its most recent quarter that market conditions would worsen in 2027 and 2028 for its clients compared with 2026. If you've followed the memory chip market during 2026, that seems like an unfathomable statement, but it's where the industry is.

SK Hynix's news that 2029 could be just as bad further extends the bull case for memory chipmakers. Furthermore, if SK Hynix is already announcing that it has sold out of capacity three years from now, high AI demand will likely continue into 2030 and 2031. As a result, there could be several years' worth of strong growth ahead for anyone involved in the memory chip space.

However, Micron has another boost up its sleeve. The company is building several new production facilities, including one scheduled to open in mid-2027, and another in late 2028 in the U.S. Internationally, Micron has two more facilities scheduled to open in 2027, and another two in 2028. So, Micron's total production capacity should be significantly expanded over the next two years, and today's market conditions will likely persist, keeping memory chip prices high.

That could cause a huge growth explosion in the company and, likewise, in the stock. However, none of this is priced into Micron's stock right now. Right now, Micron trades at 5 times fiscal year (FY) 2027 earnings.

For a long time, the stock averaged between 20 and 25 times trailing earnings. Should Micron hit estimates and rise to those levels, that would require the stock to rise 4x to 5x next year. Now, if it has another excellent 2028 and 2029, as the market outlook indicates it could, who knows where Micron's stock is headed? This requires the market to cooperate and value the stock like it did over the past year and a half. Depending on AI sentiment, this may or may not happen, but with how much growth Micron is expecting, I think market-crushing returns are easily in the cards.

The reality is that there are few stocks with as impressive a runway as Micron's. However, given Micron's cyclical history, the market is not valuing it properly. I think that will change in the next few months as the market realizes how long this AI build-out will last, and that could catapult Micron's stock to new heights. It's one of my top AI stock picks right now, and it's not too late to buy shares.

#3273. Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now, Microsoft says – here’s why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Windows > Windows 11

The latest updates to Windows 11 offer improvements in speed, performance, and memory management.

The more memory your Windows PC has, the faster it should perform, especially when juggling multiple apps, files, and other data. My laptop has 32GB of RAM, while my desktop has a hefty 64GB, and both are absolutely zippy. Does that mean computers with only 8GB of memory, or even less, are also-rans? Nope, not according to Microsoft.

Also: How much RAM does your PC really need?

In a new blog post published Tuesday, Microsoft touted the gains in speed, performance, and memory management in Windows 11 achieved by the latest updates. These especially impact PCs with just 8GB of RAM, which can now run multiple apps and files faster and more efficiently than before.

To reach this goal, the company said it had three notions in mind.

The first was to make better use of the existing memory on each Windows 11 PC. The second was to protect the tasks that need to feel instant even as more memory gets used. And the third was to ensure that key apps and Windows require less memory. Yes, a computer with 16GB, 32GB, or 64GB of RAM can better handle more intensive activities. But Microsoft wanted to make sure that systems with 8GB could also keep pace.

Based on its own lab tests of PCs with 8GB of RAM, the company claims that Windows is now 20% more responsive and that multitasking is 40% faster than before the latest updates. Here’s how.

As more memory gets allocated, Windows must move inactive apps and files from RAM to the hard drive. When you need to access those apps and files again, you have to wait for Windows to move them from disk storage back to RAM. Normally, PCs with less memory have to do a lot of this disk swapping.

One way Windows eases the pain of this process is through compression. Here, the operating system shrinks less-active data into a smaller format so it can remain in memory. Though Windows has used compression for many years, Microsoft has fine-tuned the technology to determine how much to compress, when to move data from RAM to your drive, and when to fetch it back, especially on PCs with 8GB of memory.

Also: 5 apps I always install on new Windows PCs – most are free

As such, Windows can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory rather than moving it to storage, Microsoft said. An inactive app, file, or browser that you leave open is less likely to have to reload from your hard drive when you return to it.

Opening the Start menu, launching File Explorer, right-clicking a folder or file, and searching for an item are all tasks that need to feel instant; otherwise, Windows itself feels sluggish. To achieve this on PCs with less RAM, Windows tries to prioritize certain actions you need to accomplish while backing off background tasks like search indexing, Microsoft said.

Here’s one example. After you update your computer and reboot, Windows has some housekeeping to do. But any setup work that occurs shouldn’t affect how long it takes to open an app or file.

Also: How to upgrade your ‘incompatible’ Windows 10 PC to Windows 11 – for free

The latest version of Windows 11 speeds up these types of tasks and interactions by up to 20% compared with the January 2026 version, according to Microsoft.

However, multitasking places the greatest strain on a PC with only 8GB of RAM. To analyze this, Microsoft said it conducted two tests on the same PC with 8GB of memory. One test measured the current version of Windows 11, while the other gauged the January 2026 flavor. Here, the testers opened 20 tabs in Microsoft Edge, kicked off a 4K video, and launched large files in Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, one after another. The current version of Windows is up to 40% faster than its predecessor, the company said.

To reduce the need for RAM among Windows and certain key apps, Microsoft said that it has improved how memory is managed and when it’s used.

As one example, memory is allocated to Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook more efficiently, resulting in a 360 MB savings in RAM. This maneuver also extends to third-party apps such as WhatsApp, which has reduced its memory requirements.

Also: 11 Windows apps I replace on every new PC (and the ones I keep)

On PCs with 8GB of memory, the Widgets app loads only when you open it and frees up about 200 MB of RAM when you close it. In Microsoft Edge, inactive tabs now go to sleep after 15 minutes, down from two hours previously, reducing overall memory allocation.

Across Windows, Microsoft 365, and Edge, those improvements reduced the growth in required memory by up to 900 MB, Microsoft said.

How does Microsoft test these scenarios to see whether the latest Windows updates and fixes are helping PCs with less memory?

“We test those fixes across a broader collection of over 20,000 PCs in our labs, including current 8 GB models, using automated workloads based on activities such as browsing, working in Microsoft 365 apps, joining video calls, and downloading files in the background and even using high-speed cameras to measure the time from an action, such as opening Start or launching an app, to the moment the result appears on screen,” the company explained.

Also: Why your RAM options cost 4X more now than last year

The ability to use Windows without much RAM on your PC is critical these days in light of the “RAMageddon” crisis. With AI companies scooping up massive amounts of memory and flash storage chips, remaining supply is limited, and the prices have surged. The more memory you add to a new or existing PC, the more you’re going to pay. That’s always been true, but now more than ever.

Of course, memory is only one part of the picture. Your PC’s processor and other hardware also play an important role. Here, Microsoft found that a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8GB of RAM showed 94% faster multi-core CPU performance than a 2021 8 GB model. But the same 2026 8GB PC performed on par with a 2021 16 GB system. This shows that memory does matter for multitasking, but that the processor also impacts performance.

Whether your Windows 11 PC has 8GB of RAM, less, or more, how can you take advantage of the latest enhancements? For that, you’ll want to make sure that you’ve updated to the newest version of Windows. That would be Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later, according to Microsoft. But that includes the latest optional preview build released in late October. If you don’t want to install that one, you’ll be fine with build 26300.9711 for now.

Also: The best laptops: Expert tested and reviewed

To check, head to Settings, select System, and then click About. The section for Windows Info shows the current version and build. If you need to update, stay in Settings and go to Windows Update. Assuming your PC qualifies, you should find the latest Windows 11 26H2 build ready to install.

Beyond updating Windows, you also want to keep your apps current. If you use Microsoft 365, open any app in the suite, click the File menu, select Account, click Update Options, then select Update Now.

With most other apps, you have to update them manually or individually. To ease the process, consider a good software updater program. These will automatically scan most of your installed applications to identify which need updating, then download and install the updates for you.

If you're looking for something new to watch on Netflix this weekend, I've got you covered. November is already flying by, and that means another weekend and a fresh batch of movies to check out on the streaming service.

With plenty to choose from, knowing which new arrivals are actually worth your time can be tricky. I've picked out three of the best new movies to stream, covering a few different genres to suit whatever you're in the mood for.

The list includes a festive family drama about a household trying to find its feet again, and a tense psychological thriller starring Willem Dafoe as an art thief trapped inside a luxury penthouse. There's also a crime drama following a young woman who escapes her small-town life and gets caught up in a dangerous series of cons and heists across the American South. These are the three Netflix movies I'd recommend adding to your watchlist.

Netflix kicks off its original holiday movie lineup for 2026 with "A Dog's Perfect Christmas," which is already creeping towards the No. 1 spot on the streaming service and is an ideal pick for animal lovers. Based on W. Bruce Cameron's 2020 bestselling novel, the movie continues the author's familiar approach to heartfelt animal stories. Cameron co-wrote the screenplay with director Cathryn Michon, marking another collaboration between the pair following their previous adaptations of "A Dog's Purpose" and "A Dog's Journey."

This festive family comedy follows the Goss family as they prepare for Christmas amid a difficult period. Still grieving the loss of his wife, grandfather Sander (Dennis Quaid) struggles to get along with his teenage granddaughter Ello (Brooke Lena Johnson). But when a medical emergency leaves Ello's mother in a coma, the household faces an even bigger challenge. With the help of their loyal basset hound Winstead (voiced by Thomas Haden Church) and an adorable new Corgi puppy named Ruby, the family must find a way to keep things together while hoping for a Christmas miracle.

Watch "A Dog's Perfect Christmas" on Netflix

Willem Dafoe delivers a gripping solo performance in "Inside," a psychological thriller that puts him in the middle of an increasingly tense survival story. The film also takes a darkly satirical look at the world of high-end art collecting, exploring what happens when priceless possessions become useless in a fight to stay alive. Director Vasilis Katsoupis filmed the movie in chronological order over seven weeks, helping capture the physical and psychological toll of the character's ordeal. It's a great choice if you enjoy claustrophobic thrillers.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Nemo (Willem Dafoe) is an experienced art thief who breaks into a luxurious New York penthouse to steal several valuable paintings. However, when the apartment's advanced security system malfunctions, he finds himself locked inside with no way to contact the outside world. Initially expecting his accomplices to come to his rescue, Nemo soon realizes he's been abandoned. With limited food and water, he must find increasingly inventive ways to navigate the apartment, which is filled with expensive artwork and high-tech features. As the days turn into weeks, Nemo's attempts to escape become more desperate.

"Carolina Caroline" is an indie crime thriller with a neo-noir romantic twist, bringing director Adam Carter Rehmeier and actor Kyle Gallner back together after their cult favorite "Dinner in America." Set against the dusty backroads and forgotten towns of the American South, the movie has a distinctive look, with plenty of retro vibes. It's certainly worth checking out too, especially with its impressive 90% Rotten Tomatoes score. If you enjoy offbeat crime thrillers with a strong sense of atmosphere, this one deserves a spot on your watchlist.

Caroline Daniels (Samara Weaving) is a young woman working at a gas station in rural Texas who dreams of leaving her small-town life behind. When she meets Oliver (Kyle Gallner), a charming drifter and experienced con artist, she becomes fascinated by his tricks and soon joins him on the road. The pair travel across the American South, pulling off increasingly daring scams and bank robberies while developing a passionate relationship. Along the way, Caroline hopes to track down her estranged mother in South Carolina. However, the couple soon find themselves in some dangerous situations.

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Online > Online Services

You get two subscriptions for the price of one. But the credits have some major limitations.

Lyft and DoorDash are teaming up for a new plan that essentially gives you two subscriptions for the price of one. But is it worth it?

The rideshare company announced the Lyft Go with DashPass subscription Thursday. Lyft says you’ll earn 8% back in credits to use toward your next Lyft ride or DoorDash order. Lyft Go with DashPass includes DashPass, DoorDash’s $10 monthly subscription — which includes no delivery fees and additional savings on select DoorDash orders.

Lyft is accounting for common mishaps. Lyft Go allows three trip cancellations per month and unlimited use of the Lost Item Fee Waiver in case you leave something behind in somebody’s car. Lyft currently charges $20 for drivers to make the return trip. And if you opt in to Lyft’s Round Up and Donate feature, Lyft will match 100% of your charitable donation.

Since Lyft Go with DashPass is $10 per month, you’ll basically get DashPass and Lyft Go for one price.

There’s also Lyft Go Core, a lower-tier monthly subscription that’s $5 per month. It won’t include DashPass, and you’ll earn 5% instead of 8% in credits. You’ll still get three ride cancellations and donation matching.

There are some caveats that may make you think twice. You won’t be able to earn credits through DoorDash orders and then redeem them with Lyft. And credits expire after 60 days. If you cancel your Lyft Go subscription, those credits may also expire sooner or become unavailable. And these subscriptions only work in the US. Lyft didn’t respond to a request for comment.

So if you earn credits within your free trial, you may want to use them before the trial ends if you’re considering canceling before your card is charged.

The new subscriptions give me pause given what we already know about US adults and subscriptions. CNET’s annual subscription survey found that only 10% of US adults are paying for meal and food delivery subscriptions and even fewer (3%) for automotive subscriptions.

However, subscription spending is up 23% compared to last year’s average of $1,080. Now, US adults are spending an average of $1,332 annually on subscriptions. However, most are paying for streaming services (61%), retail platforms (48%) and music (35%). If this isn’t a subscription you’ll use regularly enough to redeem the credits, it could be another subscription that sucks $10 out of your monthly budget. And you’ll need to do the math to see if the savings add up enough to justify paying for the rides, your DoorDash orders and the monthly subscription.

The new subscription comes the same day Amazon announced that Uber Eats is the new meal delivery perk after ending its GrubHub partnership.

Both Lyft Go with DashPass and Lyft Go Core are now available in the Lyft app nationwide, and a one-month free trial is available. However, if you already have DashPass, you can link your account with Lyft to have Lyft Go with DashPass at no extra cost. And if you have Lyft Pink, you’ll automatically be transitioned to Lyft Go with DashPass at no extra cost to the current price. However, Lyft Pink All-Access and Lyft Business Travel Rewards aren’t changing.

#3270. Coastal Financial: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Credit enhancements and capital discipline shielded the bank through a fintech partner crisis, a model stress-test for digital banking's durability.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Coastal Financial (CCB -1.23%) reported a return to net profitability after absorbing heavy losses from a single fintech partner program in the prior quarter. For long-term investors, the rebound demonstrates the underlying resilience of the bank's digital infrastructure model and its ability to maintain capital buffers during credit events.

The bank bounced back from a $42.1 million net loss in the second quarter by relying on partner credit enhancements, which covered nearly 97% of nonperforming loans in its Banking-as-a-Service unit (where non-bank technology firms partner with banks to offer financial products). That risk-sharing structure limited damage and helped rebuild capital reserves.

Building digital banking technology requires heavy upfront investment in software and personnel. Now management plans to prune vendor redundancies and underperforming products to expand operating margins over the next six quarters.

When regional bank Valley National Bancorp agreed to acquire partner Bluevine, it created potential deposit runoff for Coastal Financial. Management maintains extensive contingent borrowing capacity and off-balance-sheet sweep deposits, allowing it to absorb partner ownership changes without disrupting overall funding.

Platform investments in compliance and data infrastructure drive operating momentum, and the bank leverages those foundational assets to expand partner fee income. Its key advantages center on proprietary onboarding tools and credit enhancement contracts that protect the balance sheet. Management is watching expense discipline and underwriting quality across all active relationships.

Capital ratios remain strong, positioning the business to capture new partners while managing partner churn across the digital ecosystem.

#3269. I tried Sonos’ latest app features – these 2 small upgrades fix big annoyances

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Home Entertainment > Speakers

New Sonos software and firmware updates are rolling out. Here's what you can expect.

Sonos’ promise to release its AI-upgraded voice assistant is nearing its “Fall 2026” deadline, and before fans can use the highly anticipated update, the company continues to make small improvements to its app and player features.

Also: Sonos Ace Ultra vs. Sonos Ace: Who should upgrade

This time, Sonos added System Health, a new in-app page to access a more comprehensive view of your system(s), though it’s only available on iOS for now. However, a new blog post states that iOS and Android users can expect volume presets, more interaction with the app miniplayer, and spoken voice prompts for the Ace Ultra headphones.

I poked around in the app and tried some of the latest features. Here’s what to expect.

If your system consists of multiple speakers, a mix of modern and legacy speakers, or multiple systems, you’re bound to experience a hiccup and be unsure which speaker is causing the issue.

It usually takes me some time to Google my issue and scroll through the Sonos Community forum, Reddit, or the official Sonos help documents to find suggestions and troubleshoot it. Sonos’ new System Health feature provides an overview of your systems, showing your network status and name, as well as the number of speakers and rooms in each system.

Also: I used Sonos’s new home theater feature – it’s a competition killer

According to Sonos’ blog post, System Health can detect a Double Network Address issue, which usually occurs when you introduce a new router to your home or plug a mesh system into your ISP-provided router. The result is two home networks, and your Sonos speakers will split their connection between them, flagging “System not found” errors, missing speakers, or connection dropouts.

System Health is in the Settings tab, under the Help Center menu.

Once you tap into your system, you can see all of its speakers, with unconnected speakers bearing a red “Not connected” badge, and wireless speakers showing a black “Powered off” badge when they’re off.

Then, you can see a speaker’s connection information, including status, Wi-Fi signal strength, signal/noise ratio, frequency, IP address, and more. You can also find its volume output, Trueplay setup status, line-in connection, voice control status, serial number, hardware model and version, and which Sonos platform it operates on.

System Health can also show you your account details, Sonos ID, Controller ID, and your current app build version. System Health comes after Sonos updated the System Updates tab, which now displays an overview of your app, system, and headphone update status. This page also links to the Sonos release notes.

Sonos’ blog post states that this feature is new and still open to change, especially if the Sonos community has a particularly overwhelming response to it. The blog post also disclaims that this feature is a first look, not a deep dive.

However, after a brief first use, I see it as a great way to quickly access all the details you need about your systems and speakers, especially if you’re doing some rewiring, moving a speaker to a new room, or general troubleshooting.

System Health is rolling out to iOS users first. I updated my Sonos app in the App Store and was able to access it, but Sonos’ blog post states that this update is a phased rollout.

Updates to the Sonos app and its player are a long time coming. After receiving several new ways to control your speakers’ volume (I think we’re up to three), Sonos is realizing that granular volume control is a high priority for many Sonos users, including me.

The in-app volume dial is cool, and the interactive volume scrubber is a nice touch, but there’s nothing more jarring than wanting to play some tunes on my kitchen counter speaker, only for it to blast at 80% from when my husband was watching football the night before.

Sonos’ latest big update to volume this time around is Presets, a way to start playback in a specific room at a set volume. I haven’t found this feature in my app’s update yet, but I think it’s because my hardware needs an update. Presets will be available on iOS and Android.

Fortunately, I did use another update to the Sonos miniplayer: swipe to skip. What a teeny, tiny but useful feature. It works just like the miniplayer in Apple Music and Spotify; when the app is open, you can swipe left to skip to the next song.

One major caveat: swiping right to replay a track doesn’t work — at least not yet. Swiping both ways seems like a given to me, so it feels odd that you can’t. Still, being able to swipe the miniplayer to the next track is better than always having the main player open to toggle tracks. This feature is also coming to iOS and Android.

Sonos’ miniplayer is getting so much better; you can swipe to the next track and easily control volume from it, even when you have the Ace or Ace Ultra connected (I tried). The in-app volume dial also works with Sonos headphones.

Also: Sonos Play vs. Sonos Move 2: Why I’d go with the $200 cheaper Bluetooth speaker

Speaking of the Ace Ultra, a firmware update is available. A new Vocal Guidance feature can announce the battery percentage when you power on the headphones, when the audio mode changes from ANC to Transparency, and which device your headphones are connected to via Bluetooth.

It feels like this update is the final stretch before Sonos 27voice arrives, as the release notes suggest. It appears Sonos is laying the groundwork for speakers to support the AI-powered voice assistant in Early Access. Once it’s here, I’ll test it as soon as I can.

#3268. Amazon Fire TV Stick HD Review: Small, speedy, and easy on the wallet

The Amazon Fire TV Stick HD is a simple, affordable way to make a 1080p TV smarter. The new Vega OS feels quick, its slimmer design can run straight off your TV's USB port, and setup is a breeze. It's limited to 1080p and can't sideload apps like Fire OS, so if you own a 4K TV, you should spend a bit more on the new Amazon Fire Stick 4K.

Responsive, easy-to-use interface with new Vega OS

Slim design that runs off your TV's USB port

No third-party app sideloading like Fire OS

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Streaming sticks don't need to be fancy to hit their mark, and the Amazon Fire TV Stick HD is a great reminder of that. If you've got an older TV that's still going strong but has sluggish smart features (or perhaps none at all), a $35 streaming stick is an easy fix.

The 2026 Fire TV Stick HD runs Vega OS, Amazon's Linux-based software, which replaces the Android-based Fire OS that powered previous models. Amazon says the changes make it more than 30 percent faster, and it also brings a slimmer body, USB power, Wi-Fi 6 support, and free Alexa+.

It's not all pros across the board. The resolution caps out at 1080p, you can't sideload third-party apps anymore, and there's no support for Dolby Vision. But if you're shopping for a bedroom, guest room, or an older TV set that you don't primarily use, the Fire TV Stick HD is one of the cheaper streaming devices you should take a closer look at.

The Amazon Fire TV Stick HD launched on April 29, 2026, for $34.99, which is the same price as the 2024 model it replaced. It's Amazon's cheapest streaming stick, and it sits below the Fire TV Stick 4K and the Fire TV Stick 4K Max. Amazon ran a limited-time deal that brought the stick down to $21.99 shortly after launch, so we'll likely see temporary price cuts around the holiday shopping season.

Keep in mind that the stick's new "Direct Power" feature means that it gets power right from your TV's USB port. If your TV doesn't have a USB port, you'll need to pick up an adapter separately.

The Fire TV Stick HD is about as minimal as a streaming device gets, and Amazon says it's the slimmest Fire TV device the company has made. That makes it really easy to tuck behind a TV or toss in a bag for a trip, and it won't crowd the other ports and cables on your set.

The only other connection is a USB-C port for power, and thanks to "Direct Power," you can plug it straight into your TV's USB port with the included cable. That means you'll have one less wall adapter to hide, and your setup will look a lot cleaner as a result.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

The included Alexa Voice Remote covers all the basics, including voice search, menu navigation, TV power, and volume controls. It doesn't have fancy extras like a remote finder or backlit buttons, but it gets the job done. (If you want Amazon's redesigned Fire TV remote, which I liked a lot more, you'll have to get the Fire TV Stick 4K.)

Setup is about as easy as it gets. Just plug the stick into your TV's HDMI port, connect the USB-C cable to your TV's USB port, and follow the on-screen prompts. You'll then have to connect to Wi-Fi and sign in with your Amazon account, and you're off to the races.

Since Vega OS only lets you install apps from the Amazon app store, you should make sure that the ones you use most are actually available. Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Prime Video, Hulu, and other popular streaming services all run natively, but niche apps may be missing due to the lack of third-party app sideloading, which the older Fire OS allowed you to do.

The Fire TV Stick HD has a quad-core 1.7GHz processor and 8GB of storage. It can stream up to 1080p resolution with HDR10, HDR10+, and HLG, and it supports Dolby Atmos through HDMI pass-through if you have a compatible sound setup. There's no Dolby Vision here, and it won't output 4K, so it's really only meant for 1080p TV sets.

Vega OS keeps menus and home screen rows moving smoothly, and apps open quickly. I didn't have any issues switching between my most used apps on the fly. Amazon's "30 percent faster" figure is its own claim, so I wouldn't treat it as fact, but it definitely felt faster than my past Fire OS experiences.

I also like that the Fire TV Stick HD isn't limited to video. You can pair a Bluetooth game controller and play cloud games through Amazon Luna or Xbox Game Pass, which is a fun bonus, and you can even connect a pair of headphones for late-night viewing. It comes with Alexa+ free of charge, which can come in handy when you're trying to hunt down something new to watch.

The downsides are pretty familiar to past Fire TV Sticks. A big chunk of the Fire TV home screen is taken up by recommendations and sponsored content, and you'll definitely notice it (especially if you're used to Roku's cleaner layout like I am).

Sideloading third-party apps is also gone, which will bug those who liked using older Fire TV Sticks for apps that aren't available in Amazon's app store. Neither is a dealbreaker for the average viewer, but they're worth knowing about before diving in.

The Amazon Fire TV Stick HD is a fast, simple, and affordable streaming stick that's a perfect match for older HD TVs and secondary rooms. Vega OS feels speedy, the slim design and USB power keep things neat, and setup takes just a few minutes. You won't get 4K streaming resolution, Dolby Vision, or third-party app sideloading, but for $34.99 (or less on sale), it's hard to complain.

If you're looking for an alternative pick, the base model Roku Streaming Stick ($39) also tops out at 1080p, but has a cleaner interface.

In Amazon’s ecosystem, the new Fire TV Stick 4K costs $25 more, but you get 4K resolution output and a redesigned (and much better) remote. And if you're a tinkerer who wants to sideload apps, the Fire TV Stick 4K Max is the only Amazon stick that still runs Android-based Fire OS.

If you've got an older 1080p TV and want a cheap way to get streaming apps on it, the Fire TV Stick HD is a solid choice that won't break the bank.

Dylan Haas is a Freelance Contributor and Lab Tester for Tom’s Guide. He’s a seasoned journalist with bylines at publications like Mashable, GameSpot, and Paste Magazine where he covered the latest in tech, gaming, and entertainment.

#3267. What to Know About Meta’s Muse AI Before It Learns Too Much About You

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Meta’s Muse AI agent keeps a running profile of everyone who uses it. Yes, even if you deny it permission to do so. And by doing so, it’s effectively made Jolly, its “cute and cuddly” mascot, a harbinger of concerning security architecture.

Muse requests extensive access to personal data, including passwords, full disk access, email messages, calendar, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp. By default, Meta also appears to use your interactions with Muse to train its AI models, so you have to manually opt out in the settings.

If that wasn’t enough, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here’s what to know about Muse.

Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off.

The report shows that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages.

Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments.

That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

The VPN company Surfshark said it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data.

Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset for what it uncovered.

#3264. The Swift Observatory Dropped Back to Earth This Week. Here’s What to Know

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

NASA believes most of the space telescope burned up in the atmosphere, but some fragments may have made their way down to Earth.

The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, formerly known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, has reached the end of its journey. Launched into orbit in 2004, the space telescope completed an extraordinary 22-year mission when it plunged back into Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday.

“Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long,” Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of the Astrophysics Division at NASA, said in a statement last month.

NASA says the telescope hit the atmosphere Wednesday at 7:39 am ET, just four hours after the space agency predicted.

The space telescope entered orbit over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia, just west of Malaysia. NASA says that most of the space telescope likely burned up upon reentry but that some components may have survived.

In preparation for Swift’s reentry, NASA shut down operations in late October after conducting its final observation on Oct. 20. It was orbiting at just 171 miles above Earth’s surface at that point, and the increased atmospheric drag prevented Swift from doing any further work.

It was a bittersweet moment for those who worked on the project.

“It is a sad time at the Penn State Mission Operations Center, as we have carefully tended Swift to control its science operations, its health and safety, and responded to anomalies day or night, every day for 22 years,” John Nousek, director of mission operations for Swift and professor of astronomy and astrophysics at Penn State, said in an email to CNET.

Swift’s initial mission helped advance science’s understanding of gamma-ray bursts and their role in phenomena such as the birth of black holes and the history of the early universe.

That initial mission ended in 2004, but the observatory was doing so well that NASA extended its operations to continue collecting data. Its name changed to the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in 2018, in honor of pioneering NASA astrophysicist Neil Gehrels, who served as the agency’s chief of the Astroparticle Physics Laboratory from 1995 until his death in 2017.

The space telescope was designed to help solve the mystery of gamma-ray bursts by rapidly detecting them, determining their sources and then further analyzing them for study back on Earth. It also enabled unique sampling to observe newly discovered objects only minutes after their light reached Earth, Nousek said.

The volume of science research conducted using Swift’s data is difficult to match. According to NASA, Swift scanned over 2,000 gamma-ray bursts, took 1.5 million images from its ultraviolet/optical telescope and sent home 12 TB of data. That data is showcased in an estimated 7,000 research papers, which averages out to just under one study per day over its 22-year run.

“We hope Swift has set the standard for time domain astrophysics,” Nousek said.

The space telescope also helped pioneer many policies that ultimately shaped those discoveries, such as making data immediately accessible and providing over 1,000 guest investigators with the opportunity to use Swift throughout its long life.

It’s only a stroke of bad luck that kept the observatory from floating for even longer. NASA attempted a rescue of Swift over the summer of 2026. However, after a series of engineering difficulties and control issues, the attempt was abandoned, sealing Swift’s fate. NASA turned the instruments back on and kept recording data as long as possible.

#3260. SUSE lays off 1 in 10 workers – citing AI and automation

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Squarespace also announced layoffs this week, but explicit ties to AI remain inconsistent.

According to exclusive reporting by The Register, enterprise Linux provider SUSE will lay off one in 10 of its nearly 2,000-person workforce due to “automation and AI,” CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen told staff via email.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?

Van Leeuwen noted that AI is rapidly changing how software companies function.

“AI capabilities are advancing exponentially, forcing us to radically reimagine our work,” he said, adding that “the organizational design and cost base that SUSE is built on today will not carry us forward successfully.”

He did not specify which roles would be terminated, but The Register reports that staff will be notified by Nov. 4.

AI is impacting many parts of the tech industry, including open source. Just last month, Linus Torvalds announced he had used Claude Code to write a Linux patch, which Linux enthusiasts read as an evolution of his stance on AI.

By some reports, businesses are finally seeing some ROI from AI after a few years of uncertainty. But that remains localized, ironically, to tech itself. As one economist recently noted, AI has primarily increased revenue per employee at major tech companies, while leaving most other companies unchanged.

The trade-off for that growth is, at least in some cases, layoffs. But layoffs credited to AI in some way don’t mean that human roles are always being replaced. Last month, Microsoft announced it would buy out 60,000 of its workers — some of which are in its Copilot division — to prioritize AI efforts, though it’s also likely the company is reacting to spending a significant amount of money on AI infrastructure.

Jobloss.ai’s layoff tracker shows primarily tech companies — including Uber, Salesforce, and GitLab — in its recent entries, but job loss attribution to AI is still mixed, and the number of roles cut isn’t always jarringly huge.

It’s also hard to tell whether a layoff strategically frames pre-AI plans as being due to AI capabilities or is actually a result of them. That question circulated around Block’s major layoffs earlier this year. Squarespace also announced layoffs of 19% of its staff yesterday, though company communications don’t explicitly name AI. Still, vibecoding has impacted website builders overall, though Squarespace itself has invested in AI offerings.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires

Van Leeuwen’s email to staff acknowledged where SUSE has already begun to change, though it’s unclear whether he meant by adopting AI tools internally.

“Across SUSE, modern tooling is already changing our daily workflows, enabling teams to move faster with less operational overhead and flatter reporting lines. The requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished. Other roles will evolve over the next few years,” he said.

While several tech companies have announced highly visible layoffs this year that they’ve also framed as related to AI, economists agree that the massive cross-industry layoff wave many fear has yet to arrive. Gartner even predicts that companies will actually rehire 30% of the employees they tried to replace with AI — and at a higher cost — by 2029 if they don’t “overhaul workforce planning.”

Still, AI investments, vibecoding, and shifting priorities are changing the software scene overall.

Growing enrollment is critical to EPS growth, but so too is underwriting margin. In the managed care and health insurance business, underwriting margin represents the core operational profitability generated directly from managing healthcare risk. It measures the financial return an insurer achieves strictly from collecting premiums and managing medical care. On the enrollment side, ACA marketplace-driven enrollment appears poised to decline, a headwind for revenue in a segment that had been a growth driver. Fortunately, it's a smaller piece of the enterprise than Medicare and Commercial. Commercial fee-based enrollment grew ~2.9% YoY between 2024 and 2025, while total Medicare enrollment grew 4.5%.
