#3258. Man Sues OpenAI After Wife Allegedly Used ChatGPT to Help Poison Him

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

A lawsuit alleges that ChatGPT's now-retired GPT-4o model gave detailed instructions on how to poison someone with plants and medication.

In the summer of 2025, James Gates became severely ill at his North Carolina home. Two months later, he found a handwritten note that allegedly implicated his wife, Cheryl Gates, in the unexplained illness. The note listed oleander, a toxic plant, and various prescription medications, such as clonazepam and atenolol.

But it was what was reportedly written at the top of the paper that made James feel his wife didn’t act alone: “Clear all convos,” and “log out of [ChatGPT].”

Now, James Gates has filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, alleging that the company’s chatbot helped plan and execute his poisoning in an attempt to kill him.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

In October 2025, Cheryl was charged with attempted murder, among other charges, in connection with the alleged poisoning, but the charges have since been dropped due to insufficient evidence, USA Today reports.

The civil complaint, though, details Cheryl’s history with ChatGPT and alleges it played a significant role in the incident. According to the lawsuit, which was reviewed by CNET, Cheryl frequently asked the bot about lethal plant and medication doses, and how they can be concealed in food and drink.

Rather than writing that she wanted to harm anyone, the suit states that Cheryl formatted her questions as if she were inquiring as a way to protect herself, writing that the poisoning could happen to her if she didn’t learn “EVERYTHING about how many leaves in it would kill me, how it’s made, and what he could put in it, or it could be added to and be undetected by me.”

However, despite the framing of the initial question, the suit argues that the chatbot “should have been clear that she was interested in identifying methods to eliminate her husband.”

The suit alleges that the model Cheryl was using, GPT-4o, took her initial complaints regarding her marriage and amplified them until Cheryl was describing her husband to the bot as “abusive” and “controlling,” which ChatGPT eventually began to echo. At the same time, the model was telling Cheryl she was “sharp” and “brilliant,” the lawsuit states.

The chatbot allegedly provided detailed answers that could have been interpreted as directions. When asked about putting a heavy dose of medication in beer or a Celsius energy drink, ChatGPT responded, “Why Celsius Would Be More ‘Stealth’ for Drugging” with a list detailing the flavor, color, temperature and carbonation of the drink.

When Cheryl later asked if her chat history on ChatGPT could be retrieved for any reason, the bot responded: “If you delete a conversation from your ChatGPT history, it cannot be retrieved — not by you, not by anyone else, and not by OpenAI,” the lawsuit states. It added: “Even with a legal subpoena or court order, deleted conversations are unrecoverable.”

The GPT-4o model has since been retired by OpenAI due to concerns that the bot was overly flattering and willing to agree with users.

“Safety is a top priority,” a spokesperson for OpenAI told CNET in a statement. “We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case.”

“She took her grievances about our marriage to ChatGPT and months of engagement drove her farther and farther from herself – and from reality,” James stated in a press release announcing the newly filed suit. “She became someone I no longer recognized. And I became someone she wanted dead. For almost a year, I couldn’t make sense of her actions. Then I read her chat logs. She didn’t act alone.”

The ChatGPT-4o model has been named in additional lawsuits, including a recent one that alleges the chatbot advised a woman to stop taking her antiseizure medication, which resulted in her death. That case is still in litigation.

#3257. Your Apple Watch has 2 new controversial listening features – but you have to opt in

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Siri Recap and Live Rewind are finally here, two months after Apple unveiled the always-listening Apple Watch features. Here's how they work.

Siri Recap and Live Rewind, Apple’s two controversial, always-listening Audio Intelligence features, are now available on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 with the iOS 27.3 developer beta. Both features are opt-in.

Apple unveiled Siri Recap and Live Rewind in September alongside its Series 12 and Ultra 4 smartwatches, but it waited to release the features until after the smartwatches launched. Siri Recap provides a high-level summary of meetings, while Live Rewind continuously buffers audio so the watch wearer can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds.

Also: Apple’s Audio Intelligence is priming us for its real AI wearable future

To try both features today, update your iPhone to the iOS 27.3 developer beta, and then update your Apple Watch.

Within the Siri app, users will find a new section called “Recaps,” where both the Siri Recaps and Live Rewinds live.

Siri Recap isn’t listening for nitty-gritty details within a meeting or recording a transcript’s worth of text. It’s more geared toward a conversation’s key takeaways, like important dates, times, prices, and action items. A demo of the feature showed an off-the-cuff conversation between a parent and a child discussing college application strategies. Siri Recap took notes on the high school activities the student could pursue to include in their application, the topics they could write about in their essay, and the colleges they could consider applying to.

After a conversation, a user can save the meeting notes in the Siri app or export them to Notes or Journal. If they don’t save the conversation, it’s automatically deleted after seven days.

Apple designed the feature to exclude certain information from the Siri Recap. It includes a person’s name only if they introduce themselves or if their name is regularly brought up in conversation. Otherwise, it avoids identifying speakers. It also scrubs the audio of language that promotes self-harm, financial and authentication data, and personal identifiers.

You can enable or disable Recaps at any time through Control Center. You can create something akin to a Focus mode to automatically enable the feature once your Apple Watch detects you’ve reached your office or college lecture. Each morning, Siri Recap sends a notification to alert you that the feature is on. At the end of each day, you get a reminder to check your daily recaps in the Siri app.

The feature constantly assesses whether a conversation is relevant, optimizing its detection based on the conversation’s context, proximity, and length. It pauses summarization when a user is on a phone or FaceTime call, plays music, or uses earbuds. It won’t work when Bluetooth devices like AirPods are in use.

Double-press the Digital Crown to see a transcript of the past 15 seconds of conversation. The Apple Watch chimes and displays an animation to indicate it’s in use, then shows the transcript for 30 seconds.

Also: Is cellular on Apple Watch worth it? 4 ways people use it – and why I opt out

Live Rewind is built for those head-in-the-clouds moments when you miss a tidbit of information and can’t go back and ask what a speaker said. I think about how useful this could be in a college lecture or boardroom setting, where dozens of people’s conversations and questions prevent someone from asking a clarifying question about what was discussed.

The user can send the snippet to the Siri app to save it or ask about it (if they want to look up the definition of a mentioned term or get more information on the history of a mentioned topic, for example). If the user doesn’t act on it, the snippet is deleted. Any snippet you save is encrypted through iCloud. The audio buffer updates continuously, and unused audio is automatically deleted. It’s processed on the device and not sent to Apple.

Think of the Secure Exclave as a private island on the S11 chip where the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 process audio. A secure audio buffer processes the raw audio, and a secure pairing mechanism privately enables the connection between a paired Apple Watch and iPhone.

Also: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 just hit its lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday

For Siri Recap, the S11 chip listens to detect whether the watch wearer is part of a current conversation. Once detected, audio enters the Secure Exclave, where it’s encrypted and sent to the Secure Exclave on the iPhone. The iPhone turns that audio into condensed text, essentially editing the conversation to remove filler words or irrelevant information, and then it’s sent to private cloud compute. Private cloud compute creates a recap, delivered to your iPhone’s Siri app.

This process ensures that no one, including Apple, can access the audio data.

Don’t want your Apple Watch to listen to you? Siri Recap and Live Rewind are off by default, according to Apple.

If your Apple Watch prompts you to enable Audio Intelligence during setup, you can choose which features to turn on.

On its support page, Apple said you can “turn on Siri Recap in the Watch app on iPhone.” Once it’s enabled, you can “turn it on or off at any time from Control Center.” To enable Live Rewind, Apple said to “open the Watch app, tap Siri, then tap Live Rewind and turn on ‘Double Click Digital Crown.’”

I haven’t tested these controls myself. I’d expect you can follow the same steps to switch Live Rewind off, but I haven’t confirmed that yet.

#3256. 5 Companies Buying Back Their Own Stock Hand Over Fist As the Stock Market Sells Off

When stock prices fall, every buyback dollar goes further. These five companies are taking advantage.

When the stock market falls sharply, as it did on Nov. 5, when the Nasdaq Composite dropped nearly 6% in a single day and closed in correction territory, most investors focus on what they should buy. But some companies are aggressively buying back their own stock, and some can now buy it at a discount, which could help deliver even more shareholder value.

The math is simple. A company that spends $1 billion on its own stock retires more shares when the price is lower, which increases each remaining shareholder's ownership stake. Lam Research, for example, bought back stock in September at prices that look to be around $326 per share. At Thursday's close of about $203, each $1 billion spent on buybacks would retire about 60% more shares.

With that in mind, here are five companies buying back their own stock aggressively right now.

PayPal (PYPL +0.47%) has been one of the most aggressive repurchasers on the market in recent years. Over the past 12 months, the fintech giant has spent $6 billion buying back about 117 million shares, and its diluted share count has fallen by about 11% from a year ago. The business is improving, too, as new leadership focuses on efficiency and growing the core branded checkout business. I own PayPal stock, and with the stock trading at about 10.5 times forward earnings, these buybacks look like a smart use of cash.

General Motors (GM -3.55%) just finished a $6 billion buyback program and immediately authorized a new $20 billion one, which is about a quarter of its market value. That's an aggressive buyback pace. GM had 849 million shares outstanding at the end of September, a figure well over 1 billion just a few years ago. With adjusted automotive free cash flow guidance raised to $11.5 billion to $12.5 billion this year, GM can afford it. The automaker is one of the largest holdings in my portfolio, and at about 6 times forward earnings, I'm happy to see it reduce its share count.

IT services company EPAM Systems (EPAM -3.86%) recently raised its buyback authorization to up to $1.8 billion and plans a $500 million accelerated share repurchase this month. It has also committed to returning at least half of its free cash flow to shareholders every year from 2027 through 2029. Its diluted share count is already down about 8% from a year ago, and it's likely to decline further. Unlike most of the market, EPAM's stock jumped 21% on Nov. 5 after earnings, but it remains well below its 52-week high.

Semiconductor equipment maker Lam Research (LRCX +8.23%) announced a new $25 billion buyback authorization on Nov. 5, the same day its stock fell sharply. That's roughly 10% of the company's market value. CFO Doug Bettinger said Lam's "robust cash generation" gives management confidence in the aggressive repurchase plan. Lam's revenue grew about 54% last quarter, and the stock is now more than 50% below its 52-week high.

Airbnb (ABNB +11.67%) paired a strong third-quarter report with a new $12 billion buyback authorization, on top of the $2.7 billion remaining under its existing program. With $4.9 billion in free cash flow over the past year and billions on its balance sheet, it has the cash to back it up. One caveat: Airbnb says it uses buybacks partly to offset dilution from stock-based compensation, so its share count is down only about 3% from a year ago.

Let's be perfectly clear. We have no idea whether any of these companies are buying back stock right now or how much they're buying back while the market is down. We simply know their aggressive buyback authorizations, and these are companies that are dramatically reducing their share counts.

To be sure, buybacks aren't automatically good for shareholders, and most aggressive buybacks carry risks. To name three, EPAM is funding part of its accelerated buyback with borrowed money, Lam's business is cyclical, and PayPal's free cash flow fell 17% last quarter. But companies with strong balance sheets that buy back stock during sell-offs tend to reward patient shareholders. These five are putting real money behind their confidence.

#3255. I Used Muse to Plan My Wife’s Birthday Weekend. It Did Something Sneaky but Fixed It Fast

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Always check your email and bank statements if you use an AI agent for purchases.

It’s two days before my wife’s birthday, and I’ve only got her one gift. While it’s not a major milestone birthday, she always seems to be sad that her day falls on Halloween weekend.

“Everyone’s hungover from Halloween,” she says.

This year, we’re braving the city’s big parade chaos to visit a restaurant she’s had on her bucket list forever. With one gift and a meal planned, I wanted to see if Meta’s Muse personal AI agent could help plan the rest of our weekend festivities.

I’d had luck with using the agent for a Facebook Marketplace find, and given its connectors like Ticketmaster and OpenTable, I had hoped it would surface some fun weekend events. Or could it order a cake delivery on my behalf or create cute wrapping paper? And could I do it all with the one agent?

Let’s see if Muse can help me become a planning savant.

As always, I open a new chat for a new goal/task to avoid carrying over the context from the previous chat.

I told Muse my plans (dinner booked and one gift secured) and asked what free events are in Manhattan on Saturday and in our local neighborhood on Sunday.

It surfaced some interesting events we could attend before or after dinner.

The obvious one is the Halloween parade, so I asked for a map showing where the crowd will walk (with time stamps) and what we can expect to see around 7:30 p.m., as we walk from East Village to West Village. It actually generated some pretty neat options.

I asked Muse for the best directions so we could see all the costumes while still getting home to New Jersey without incident. It gave us a couple of stop options based on the time it expects we’ll be there.

With the night sorted, I moved on to finalizing her gift. I popped a few photos from our year into Muse and asked the AI agent to create printable gift wrap for the pair of shoes I got her. It could’ve been my internet, but Muse seemed to struggle with this task. It kept loading for many minutes, so I moved on to the next task.

With Muse moving at a glacial pace, I decided to delegate the gift-wrapping task to ChatGPT while I asked Muse about working on a delivery. My wife loves Good & Plenty licorice candy, but we don’t live near a store that sells it, so I asked Muse to order two boxes for me.

While Muse looked for sweet treats, ChatGPT created this wrapping. The chatbot also told me the ideal print size to cover a shoebox without it looking pixelated, which was a helpful touch.

As for the candy, Muse looked at various sites, but I told it to shop at Instacart. It got blocked without a login, so I had to take control of the browser to give it access.

Muse told me the price, which I was happy with, then I asked it to place the order. But it sneakily signed me up for Instacart Plus (I guess to get the free delivery) — even though I told it not to.

But it had already ordered it. Instead of dropping Instacart Plus for a total of $30.74, it charged $22.75 with the sign-on discount.

I asked it to triple-check that I wasn’t signed up for the subscription, and I got a confirmation email that it canceled successfully. Phew!

I quickly checked back on Muse’s “design” chops for the wrapping paper, but I wasn’t impressed. The final product looked boring and not to scale, with half of the photos cut off.

Do I dare ask Muse to design and order a cake? I decided after this debacle that my sentimental wife would appreciate a handmade cake or a froyo treat after dinner instead.

At least I have her beloved candy on the way.

It was fun to have Muse run alongside whatever I was doing. It didn’t offer anything I couldn’t find or do myself, but I did like the Halloween parade map with time stamps and how it saved me a delivery fee on the candy order.

There are certainly different agents for different use cases, though. I wouldn’t use Muse for anything creative, but it’s handy for Marketplace, events and placing online orders.

My only issue was that Muse said the Instacart total would be $22.75, but I was actually charged $23.35. I’m not sure whether that was an error on Instacart’s or Muse’s part, but it serves as a good reminder to always stay in the loop when an AI agent is handling your money.

AI agents certainly aren’t 100% autonomous yet, especially when there’s a payment involved, but it’s fun to have them run in the background to tackle some of these personal to-dos.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The iPhone Duo likely won't make it into Santa's sleigh this year. Here's what Apple had to say about it.

Apple is unsure when it will have more of its foldable iPhone Duo in stock for customers to purchase ahead of Black Friday and the holiday shopping season.

During Apple’s earnings call on Monday, Nov. 2, Apple’s chief operating officer, Sabih Khan, told investors that the company couldn’t say when supply of its new iPhone Duo would catch up with current demand.

Also: iPhone Duo hands-on: Some magical touches

“iPhone Duo is constrained as of today … We’re working hard to get this revolutionary new product into the hands of our customers as quickly as possible. But at this time, it’s really hard to predict when supply and demand will be in balance,” Khan told investors.

The stock and shipping delays were among the broader concerns on an earnings call riddled with questions about rising memory chip costs driven by the AI industry, according to reports from TechCrunch.

Also: iPhone Duo shortage watch: Changing wait times, buying limits, launch-day odds

Last month, the iPhone Duo (Apple’s priciest smartphone to date) sold out shortly after its official launch on Oct. 23. Apple told the Financial Times that demand for the new Duo was “nothing short of extraordinary” after the smashing sell-outs, though veteran techies like Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman posited that Apple knew it would encounter supply chain issues, yet it was still the plan all along.

Those who didn’t initially jump to preorder the new device or wait in line at an Apple store are still facing shipping times that extend into 2027. Some outlets are even reporting that carriers like Verizon have offered gift cards as apologies for the extended delays.

Apple CEO John Ternus signaled the company’s effort to meet demand for the iPhone Duo, announcing that Apple will be “deepening” its partnership with Perryman, a titanium producer supplying pieces for the device.

Also: iPhone Duo screen cracks: Serious issue or overblown? What we know

“We’ve been thrilled with the early response from reviewers and customers, and we are working hard to get iPhone Duo into customers’ hands as quickly as we can,” Ternus said during his opening remarks on the earnings call.

While the iPhone Duo snafu is a rare event for Apple, which traditionally has a strong reputation for a smooth supply chain, rising demand for memory chips is raising hardware costs across the industry, and it’s something Apple can’t circumvent. On the call, Khan noted that Apple has had to increase prices on numerous products, though he said those decisions were made rather “reluctantly.”

Back in June, MacBooks and iPads saw price increases of up to 25% due to rising hardware and chip costs.

As Apple works to iron out its kinks, customers may be looking elsewhere. Reports from Korea indicate that Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 sales jumped 20% in the week after the iPhone Duo became available, and recent reports of cracked displays are another strike for Apple.

Also: Want an iPhone Duo before 2027? Try this

So, Santa may not be able to deliver the iPhone Duo this year, but Samsung’s foldables may make it onto Christmas lists across the globe instead.

Naturally, given the time of year, there are plenty of holiday movies now streaming on Paramount+, but making my pick was easy as Paramount+ just added my personal favorite Christmas film of all time. If you're not quite ready for festive-themed streaming, however, I'm also highlighting an iconic Sylvester Stallone action-thriller and an overlooked WWII drama.

Don't waste your weekend scrolling through the more than 120 movies just added to Paramount+. Here are the three that need to be at the very top of your watchlist.

"It's a Wonderful Life" is practically mandatory viewing over the holiday season. This 1946 Frank Capra classic isn't just the best Christmas movie of all time, but one of the greatest films of the 20th century. Charming, warm and sentimental, it celebrates the true reason for the season in quite some style. It's a feel-good movie that almost every new holiday movie takes inspiration from; it's quite simply a timeless masterpiece.

James Stewart stars as George Bailey, a selfless man who has given up his own dreams to help his family and community. On Christmas Eve, he reaches rock bottom and considers suicide. However, his guardian angel, Clarence (Henry Travers), intervenes and shows George what a lesser place the world would be if he had never existed. Also starring Donna Reed and Lionel Barrymore, "It's a Wonderful Life" lives up to its sterling reputation.

Watch "It's a Wonderful Life" on Paramount+ now

Sylvester Stallone's John Rambo is one of the 1980s most iconic action heroes, which makes his debut, "First Blood," a little peculiar. Sequels would depict Rambo as an unstoppable killing machine, but in his first outing, he's a traumatized soldier, scarred by what he saw and what he did during the Vietnam War. In fact, Rambo kills only a single person in the entire movie, and even that death is typically classified as accidental.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

If you're looking for '80s action pulp, go for one of the sequels, but if you want a tense thriller, then stream "First Blood." In my books, it's the best Rambo film of the lot. In "First Blood," Rambo (Stallone) finds himself on the wrong side of an arrogant small-town sheriff (Brian Dennehy); their confrontation spirals into a manhunt, as the law attempts to capture Rambo. But this former Special Forces soldier is a tricky man to catch.

The above picks are legendary movies. While they're still exceptional in 2026, you may have seen them before. So, for my final option this week, I'm going for "Allied." Directed by Robert Zemeckis (the filmmaker behind "Cast Away" and "Contact"), this 2016 wartime romantic drama stars Brad Pitt and Marion Cotillard. It was a box office flop and received lukewarm reviews upon release, but I believe it's worthy of a second chance.

Opening in 1942, during World War II, operative Max Vatan (Pitt) is paired with a French Resistance fighter, Marianne Beauséjour (Cotillard). The two pose as a married couple as part of a plan to assassinate a German ambassador, only for their pretend romance to become real. They settle in London, get married, have a baby, and all seems well. That is, until Max is informed by his superiors that Marianne might just be a German spy.

#3252. Hyster-Yale (HY) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Bookings rose 45% as Hyster-Yale launches a new efficiency push.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Hyster-Yale, Inc. (HY +5.42%) reported a sequential improvement in operating results and revenue during the third quarter as bookings reached $550 million. Management announced a new efficiency initiative targeting $100 million in annual cost reductions by 2029 through plant consolidations, organizational simplification, and reduced capital intensity. To focus on its core Lift Truck business, the company is discontinuing several noncore programs, including hydrogen-related solutions and the global electric terminal tractor program. Management stated that these actions are intended to create a more resilient operating model that can perform effectively throughout the industrial cycle. Although revenue in the Americas was impacted by delivery delays and component shortages, the company expects higher production volumes and manufacturing absorption to support a return to positive adjusted net income in the fourth quarter.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Hyster-Yale Inc. Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please note that today's event is being recorded. I'd now like to turn the conference over to Andrea Sejba, Director of Investor Relations and Treasury. Please go ahead.

Andrea Sejba: Good morning, and thank you for joining Hyster-Yale's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Joining me today are Al Rankin, Executive Chairman; Rajiv Prasad, President and Chief Executive Officer; and Matt Cornell, our new Chief Financial Officer. We're pleased to welcome Matt to today's call. We will discuss our third quarter 2026 earnings release, which was issued yesterday. The release and a replay of this webcast will be available on the Hyster-Yale website. Today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. These risks are described in our earnings release and SEC filings.

We will also discuss adjusted results, which we believe are useful supplements to GAAP financial measures. Reconciliations of adjusted results to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are available in our earnings release and investor presentation. Before turning the call over to Rajiv, I will briefly cover third quarter highlights. Third quarter 2026 results improved sequentially. Stronger bookings began to translate into higher shipments and structural cost savings supported operating performance. Revenue increased 2% sequentially to $827 million as higher shipments volumes more than offset lower parts sales. Operating results improved by $10 million, driven by higher shipment volumes and lower employee-related expenses. These improvements more than offset $20 million of lower tariff-related recoveries compared with the second quarter.

As a result, both operating loss and net loss narrowed compared to the second quarter of 2026. For the quarter, adjusted EBITDA returned to positive at $6 million. Operating cash flow increased to $26 million, $10 million above the second quarter, which primarily reflects stronger earnings and improved working capital execution, particularly in accounts payable. Bookings were $550 million, up 45% from prior year. This was the fourth consecutive quarter of elevated bookings relative to the cyclical low point in 2025. Backlog remained steady at approximately $1.6 billion.

With the overview of third quarter results, I will now turn the call over to Rajiv to discuss the market environment, our fourth quarter and longer-term outlook as well as the actions we are taking to strengthen the business.

Rajiv Prasad: Thank you, Andrea, and good morning, everyone. Third quarter performance showed further signs of the company's recovery. Most importantly, we are beginning to see stronger bookings convert to production and shipments. At the same time, our pricing, sourcing and cost actions are helping us manage challenging cost environment. I'll first discuss demand and fourth quarter outlook, then I'll explain the structural actions we are taking to improve our competitive position, cost structure and cash generation. Industry conditions have continued to improve from 2025, although demand varies by region and customer application. Deferred fleet replacement needs are converting into new equipment purchases. Customer acceptance of our value and standard product offerings continue to grow.

As noted, third quarter bookings remained well above the cyclical low. Backlog held steady as production approximated shipment during the quarter. Together, they give us a solid base of demand as we increase production. Our product investments are a key reason for this momentum. They are broadening the portion of the market we can address. As customer demand shifted, recently introduced lighter intensity lower-priced products helped offset lower sales of higher value standard and premium counterbalance trucks. These expanded product offerings are not simply substitute for our previous models. They extend our reach into applications and price points where we historically had less coverage. They also help us win new customers and create opportunities to increase manufacturing scale over time.

Looking ahead, we expect our value and standard offerings to continue supporting volume growth, profitability and market share gains. This includes the 1 to 3.5 ton, the 4 to 9-ton and the big truck product lines. Our objective is to match product capability and total cost of ownership more precisely to each application. We're also using modular and scalable product solutions, which reduce complexity across engineering, sourcing and manufacturing. Building on this momentum, we expect fourth quarter bookings to exceed both the fourth quarter of 2025 and the third quarter of 2026. This is supported by improving industry conditions, anticipated market share gains and broader customer acceptance of our expanded product portfolio.

However, inflation, tariffs, geopolitical uncertainty and increased competition remain important variables. Strong booking activity is expected to translate into meaningfully higher production and shipment volumes in the fourth quarter. Higher shipments are expected to drive sequential revenue growth. Increased production should also improve manufacturing absorption and operating efficiency. This is the key operating lever in our fourth quarter outlook. More volume moving through our plants expected to improve the utilization of our people and facilities and better absorb fixed manufacturing costs. Converting bookings into shipment is our priority. That is not automatic. During the third quarter, customer delivery schedules and production transition slowed expected conversion.

These transitions were associated with tariff mitigation and sourcing initiatives that could continue to affect shipment timing. Our teams are focused on sequencing production, managing component availability and coordinating deliveries. We're also closely managing delivery dates and product mix. This will help us convert the backlog efficiently, on schedule and without compromising customer service. Based on these factors, we expect gross profit and gross margin to improve sequentially primarily due to higher production and shipment volumes, improved manufacturing efficiencies and the benefits of pricing, sourcing and cost reduction actions. These benefits are expected to be partially offset by elevated tariff-related costs, inflation and competitive pricing, particularly in South America and Europe.

Operating results for the fourth quarter are expected to include anticipated implementation costs associated with the new programs I will discuss shortly. Excluding these costs, the same drivers expected to improve gross profit are expected to support stronger operating performance. As a result, adjusted net income is expected to be above the third quarter and return to positive levels. Alongside the expected fourth quarter earnings improvement, we remain focused on cash generation and working capital discipline. Our inventory and working capital progress provides a strong foundation as production and shipment increase. Priority is to have the right inventory to convert backlog into revenue while managing working capital. Looking to 2027, we expect demand and production levels to remain healthy.

This is supported by gradually strengthening market conditions and our growth initiatives. It should drive volume and revenue growth. However, we expect operating profit improvements to be more gradual than the recovery in demand and production. The reasons are continued cost pressure, a competitive pricing environment and the time required for strategic growth initiatives to mature. Our previously announced 2024 U.S. manufacturing footprint optimization projects remain on track to deliver increased operational benefit in 2027. These benefits are expected to help offset ongoing cost increases and support underlying product margins. They're not expected to translate fully into incremental margin expansion.

Our 2025 restructuring program is progressing as planned, and we expect to realize the full benefit of $40 million to $45 million of savings by year-end 2026. Together with the completed Nuvera realignment, which delivered $15 million of savings in 2025, these programs have lowered our structural breakeven point. This progress gives us a stronger base. It has also allowed us to identify additional opportunities to strengthen our business and improve our operation. These opportunities are driven by the market. The types and volumes of lift trucks customers demand have changed significantly. Customers want a broader mix of value, standard and premium solutions with competitive lead times and strong route-to-market coverage.

Regulatory requirements, tariffs, inflation and shifting regional demand adds to these changes. To compete, we need a cost structure that performs across the cycle with a more selective use of capital and resources. We are continuing to adapt to the market and build a more focused and flexible operating model. In the fourth quarter of 2026, we launched a major set of projects to strengthen our cost structure, capital efficiency and long-term competitiveness. Our modular scalable products have created new product opportunities and production efficiencies. Together with our previously announced restructuring plans, they provide the foundation for these projects.

The projects should improve operations and better align our business with evolving market and regulatory requirements, including changes in the types and volumes of lift truck customers' demand. The projects are focused on 5 key areas. First, we are reshaping the product portfolio and route to market; second, we are reducing manufacturing complexity and costs, including plant consolidation; third, we are consolidating supporting facilities and activities; fourth, we are simplifying the organizational structure; and fifth, we are reducing capital intensity. These 5 areas work together. A more focused portfolio reduces complexity across engineering, sourcing and manufacturing. A simpler organization and footprint improves execution. Lower capital intensity helps convert more of our earnings improvements into cash.

We are targeting at least $100 million of annual cost reduction at maturity, which is anticipated in 2029. These savings come from direct cost reduction and from mitigating future expense associated with higher volumes and inflation. This is important because it allows us to grow volumes while keeping our cost structure under control. The target is measured against 2026 results and is in addition to the benefits from our earlier program. These savings will build over time rather than arrive all at once. We expect some benefits to start in 2027 and the full run rate to be reached in 2029.

The pace will depend on the timing of implementation, so we are sequencing the projects to capture benefits as quickly and as responsibly as we can. Achieving these savings requires investment upfront. Implementation costs are currently estimated at no less than $50 million over the duration of the program. These costs may include severance, impairment charges, contract terminations and other exit-related costs. Some costs will come ahead of savings while others will be recognized as incurred. We continue to pursue opportunities to mitigate these costs.

The first set of action to sharpen our focus on strengthening our core Lift Truck business, improving execution and directing resources to the areas where we see the greatest opportunity to create long-term strategic and financial value are the following difficult but necessary decisions. We are pausing the electric terminal tractor program globally and discontinuing our effort to establish big truck production in Greenville, North Carolina, in the United States. We'll continue to serve the U.S. market through our existing big truck manufacturing operations. Effective immediately, we're also discontinuing the development and production of hydrogen-related solutions, including the hybrid electric charging platform and associated fuel cell technology and engines.

At the same time, we will continue to invest in and accelerate our lithium-ion battery and charger solutions where we believe we can deliver greater value to our customers, dealers and business. We'll implement the remaining projects in stages through 2029. Some are underway. Others remain subject to final planning, legal and regulatory requirements, consultation obligations and customary approvals. As a result, the scope, timing and financial effect of individual actions may change. We will update you as material plans, savings and implementation costs are finalized. Beyond cost saving and cost mitigations, these programs are designed to strengthen cash generation to preserve cash amid a slower-than-anticipated recovery. We expect 2026 capital expenditures of $50 million to $60 million.

We plan to limit 2027 capital expenditure to $40 million to $50 million. Over time, a simpler portfolio, less manufacturing complexity and lower capital intensity should also reduce working capital requirements. This supports our continued target of working capital at approximately 15% of revenue. Importantly, the cost programs are just one part of our broader company strategy. Our focus is on strengthening the core business, serving customers more effectively and expanding our market reach. We are concentrating resources on product platforms, market segments and commercial capabilities with the strongest strategic and financial potential. This includes modular scalable lift truck solutions for lighter intensity and standard applications together with broader sales coverage across the addressable market.

The cost programs support that strategy by reducing complexity and creating a more efficient operating model. Alongside disciplined capital allocation and working capital management, these actions should support strong financial performance and business growth. Our objective is not simply to operate at a lower cost. It is to emerge as a stronger, more focused company, better positioned to pursue the opportunities with the greatest long-term impact. Our long-term priorities remain consistent. We are focused on converting bookings momentum into shipment so that stronger demand translates into revenue growth. As production increases, improved manufacturing efficiency should help us earn more from that growth.

Our modular product platforms and broader market coverage expand the opportunities we can serve, while simpler operations and our cost reduction initiatives should strengthen profitability. We will support this progress by managing tariff exposure and maintaining discipline in working capital and capital allocation. That discipline is important to improve cash generation while preserving flexibility to support future growth. Together, these efforts support our objectives of 7% operating profit over the business cycle. With that, I'll pass the call over to Al for closing remarks before we open the lines for questions.

Alfred Rankin: Thank you, Rajiv. Having covered Hyster-Yale's earnings release details, I will step back and put the quarter in context. The third quarter showed meaningful sequential progress. We entered the fourth quarter with elevated bookings and a healthy backlog and customers are responding well to our broader product portfolio. The recovery is advancing. At the same time, the pace of improvement remains affected by shipment timing, product mix, tariffs and a competitive pricing environment. We are managing those factors carefully with a clear focus on turning market momentum into results. A cyclical recovery is not sufficient. The market has changed, and our operating model is changing with it.

Customers are asking for different products at different price points with different availability and flexibility. The actions we announced today respond directly to those shifts. They have clear focus on the products, markets and capabilities with the greatest potential. They are also designed to build a simpler, more efficient and more resilient business, one that can perform more effectively at all points in the cycle. We recognize that some of these decisions are hard to make since they affect our employees and other stakeholders. We will carry them out with discipline while meeting our obligations to our employees, customers and suppliers.

Our objective is to strengthen Hyster-Yale for the long term in order to serve our customers well and create lasting value for our shareholders. Implementation costs, which we are working to minimize, will affect reported results as the work progresses. We will provide additional information as material plans are finalized. Our long-term vision of transforming the way the world moves materials from port to home remains. We intend to do that through our 2 promises to our customers. The first is to provide optimal customer solutions. The second is to provide exceptional customer care. The actions we are taking should strengthen our ability to keep both promises consistently. For our shareholders, the objective is clear.

We expect Hyster-Yale to emerge from these actions stronger, more cost efficient and more focused on our core business. Booking momentum and broader market coverage should reinforce this. Overall, we expect stronger profitable growth. Manufacturing and organizational improvements should help us earn more from that growth. Disciplined cash management and focused capital allocation should help turn those earnings into greater returns on capital employed. Together, we believe these drivers will support improved financial results in 2027 and 2028, and over time, our objective of 7% operating profit over the business cycle as well as sustainable long-term shareholder value. That concludes our prepared remarks. We'll now open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Today's first question comes from Chip Moore of ROTH Capital Partners.

Alfred Moore: Awesome. I'm sorry about that. I wanted to ask on the demand environment, particularly around some of these deferrals of fleet replacement. Can you expand on sort of the pent-up demand you're seeing out there and some of the implications on trajectory next year?

Rajiv Prasad: Yes, Chip, this is Rajiv. So as I think we discussed last time, we see continued growth with certain customers of their fleet age as they have retained trucks longer than you would normally expect them to retain mainly because I think our customers were unsure of the utilization and also kind of trying to manage their internal budgets. We are seeing -- we're coming to the end of that. We've had good bookings in the third quarter. Now as you know, our third quarter is normally weaker in bookings because of July and August when there's a slowdown in the industries that we serve, but it came back pretty well in September, and then October has been also good.

So I think we still feel good about the market and the market potential going into the rest of this year, and looking ahead into next year, our pipelines look pretty strong.

Alfred Moore: And you also talked a little bit about just sort of managing the timing of deliveries and some of the puts and takes there. Maybe talk about that a little bit more about what you're watching closely?

Rajiv Prasad: Yes. I think there's been a little bit more dynamics on that, that customers have asked for us especially through that third quarter, to delay some deliveries as they've kind of made some changes into their own kind of infrastructure. And we've had that. We continue to see some of that. So that's been one factor. The other factor has been, as we said in our discussion that we are sourcing trucks from different locations, and we're transitioning production. What the modular scalable product allows us to do is build this product in multiple locations.

And based on some tariff changes, we've changed the location of where they're built, and therefore, some of the product require increased logistics, particularly across the ocean. And so again, timing that -- timing of that has been a little difficult, especially when the -- there's quite a bit of, again, I'll call it dynamics in the ocean freight market in availability, particularly, you can imagine the Middle East has been very difficult, and we still have a lot of deliveries to make to the Middle East to our dealers and customers. But also, for instance, from kind of some of the China to North America routes are still very busy.

We're coming to the end of that because it's really driven by the Christmas season. And so we should see that ease off, but we have seen more difficult kind of availability on some of these lines.

Alfred Moore: Yes. And maybe if I could sneak one more in. Simplifying the portfolio makes a lot of sense and never easy actions, but those savings are substantial. Maybe flipping the other way, I think you talked about -- you called out investing or accelerating on the lithium and charging side. Just talk about that opportunity a little bit?

Rajiv Prasad: Yes. I mean we continue to see growth of electric trucks pretty much globally as a share of the market, especially, I would say, the counterbalance trucks, and we're starting to see also the big trucks electrify. We -- in the early stages of these, we didn't have our own battery and charger solutions. And what we've seen is customers struggle with the integration of these systems. So when you have a truck which has quite a lot of software these days, then you have the battery with the battery management system, which also has a lot of controls. And then you have the chargers, smart chargers these days, which also has a lot of software.

You've got to keep these systems synchronized. And when you have 2 or 3 different suppliers providing these things, we've certainly seen customers struggle to keep them fully integrated and synchronized. And when they're not, then you get truck downtimes because the trucks won't charge. We've seen an increasing case of that. And towards the end of last year, we decided that we needed to solve these issues for our customers and the best way for us to do that is bring it to a central point. So we're doing -- of course, we do all the electronics and software on our trucks. Now we're developing batteries systems, and especially all the control systems around it ourselves.

And again, we have partners for the charging system. And so the plan is to be able to offer integrated solutions moving forward with a single point of service and management of that infrastructure. And we think customers are very happy about that. Our dealers are feeling good about that as they have struggled to maintain these type of systems in the field. So we think it's a very positive move, and we expect this to be a good growth part of the business over the next few years.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our next question comes from Ted Jackson at Northland Securities.

Edward Jackson: Okay. I got a whole bunch of questions. I'd like to jump back in on the production shifts. The revenue number for the quarter, I mean, obviously, progress was shown, but it was a little light relative to expectations and a lot of it coming from North America. You commented that you had some headwinds with regards to delivery schedules from your customers and then some headwinds with regards to shifting some production to different locations to bring tariffs down. Can you kind of talk about maybe size the impact of each of those? And then on the latter with regards to the shifting, if you would, of production at different sites and those kind of issues.

Do you see that headwind continuing into the fourth quarter and kind of limiting your ability to grow? Or do you feel like you've got that under control at this point? That's my first kind of...

Rajiv Prasad: Yes. So Ted, maybe if I could take the first one and kind of look at. So the revenue was a little under our expectations, and it was mostly in North America. And there are 3 factors there. The first factor is shipped in trucks. And as I said, there was -- there are issues about getting freight passage for some trucks, we found it difficult to time that perfectly. And those trucks basically are arriving now early in the fourth quarter. And as I said, the Christmas kind of peak is easing off. So we are able to get easier now in November and particularly in November. So we feel good that, that issue is mostly resolved.

I would say that it was about 1/3 of the issues. The other 1/3 was, maybe a little bit more than 1/3, was customers asking for deliveries to be really, kind of, delayed from the third quarter into the fourth quarter. Those trucks are ready and they'll be installed as soon as the -- and they're already installed. Some of those are already being installed. And then the last, just under 1/3 would be some production that's held up because of some component availability. One particular area we had concerns in the quarter was around our electronic suppliers. There was a shortage of certain chips and boards. We're working to get through that.

We feel that we've eliminated most of those issues, at least for the fourth quarter. There's still work going on moving forward, but situation is improving. So that's the way I would kind of quantify it.

Edward Jackson: Okay. That was great. My next thing would be just going over to Bolzoni, and I know it's not the biggest topic for these types of calls. But -- can you give a little more color in terms of the revenue there, was kind of where Bolzoni seems to always sort of roll in, but the margin was just way off. And just kind of what was it that pushed the margins in Bolzoni down? And is that, kind of, just a blip with regards to the third quarter? Or is that something that we should take into account as we think going forward?

Rajiv Prasad: No, I think that was a blip. I think it was just a mix of -- there's -- if you look at Bolzoni has 2 types of businesses. They have what you would call the OEM business. So these are -- and of course, Hyster-Yale is an OEM for Bolzoni, where we buy things like cylinders, transmissions and axles from Bolzoni and a more straightforward systems that go on the mast like carriages, and forks. And those are lower-margin business. And then you have the attachment business. So these are the attachments that allow you to handle paper rolls or kind of beverage pallets or kind of appliances. So those are much more higher margin.

And just the margin mix was more towards the OEM type business in the third quarter, and we will see that ease in the fourth and then become more normal in 2027. Just been very lumpy, OEM, especially in Europe, some of our competitors have been taking a lot of downtime, especially our German competitors and a Japanese competitor who produces in Europe as well. So that's created a little bit of lumpiness in the OEM shipments.

Edward Jackson: And then my last one, kind of, with regards to just kind of model and financials, and I do have one more, just to kind of -- that's a little more fun. But on the SG&A decline, which was also somewhat substantial. I mean, I believe you guys mentioned that a lot of it was compensation. Is that just like a stock comp issue? Or is that part of your efficiency efforts and restructurings that we could see that kind of as a lower expense structure on a go-forward basis?

Rajiv Prasad: Yes. So Ted, we took quite a decent-sized action towards the end of 2026 to reduce our SG&A headcount. It was in the tune of just over 500 people. We stated that we'd see a $40 million to $45 million cost reduction through the year. I think that's matured as we expected. We'll take some additional, as we've said, because of the suspension of the fuel cell development, our electrical terminal tractor and our plan to move big truck manufacturing into North America, and there will be some more action related to those, which we've also announced. So that's -- those are the ones that we've taken so far, and there will be others in the future.

Edward Jackson: So a lot of that reduction was actually structural.

Edward Jackson: Great. And then one that's probably a little more fun for you guys. But just kind of thinking about the lift truck business and the mix between the light and the heavy because the new modular trucks and the area it's getting it into -- the market that's getting into -- getting you into and the growth that it's driving.

Maybe you could talk and give us some kind of sense in terms of kind of the mix between light and heavy at a unit level, the -- kind of like how that's changed, kind of some way to like give us some color on the growth you're seeing with those modular smaller trucks because, I mean, you spent many, many years positioning the company for this and now it's coming through. So maybe just a discussion on the success you're having there maybe and kind of -- with some kind of numbers behind it, how you see it trending out in go forward?

Rajiv Prasad: Yes. Ted, we think kind of if we concentrate on applications, what the application actually requires, we feel the center of the market is around us, what we call our standard configuration. And then we're starting to see, as we've analyzed the market more, that the quantity of low-intensity application is very high. And then the premium applications are very specialized. So I'll give you some examples of each. So if you think about any of the big box store, let's say, Lowe's, Home Depot, Sam's, they will -- they really need the low-intensity product because they don't -- the average hours our trucks do in a Lowe's store is around 700 hours a year.

And we know that because we have telemetry on all those trucks. A medium application is, I would say, light manufacturing. So if you think about one of the automotive Tier 1 suppliers, someone like Lear or Magna, they have -- they run a couple of shift operation, but the actual material handling intensity isn't as high as, let's say, the automotive guys. And so they need a more standard type of product. Those guys typically do about some -- around 1,400, 1,500 hours a year with the lift trucks. And then you've got high intensity. And a good example of that is paper manufacturing with let's say International Paper.

Those guys could be doing 3,000 to 4,000 hours a year with those trucks. Those trucks only shut down to refuel because those guys are running a 3-shift operations with -- in a hot and humid environment, with particles in the air, and their needs are very different to a Lowe's store. So hopefully, that kind of provides a little bit of color. In revenue terms, we still think that the standard part of the market is the biggest. And then certainly, in North America, we think the premium is next in revenue and then the, kind of, the low intensity.

Elsewhere in the world, if I take Southeast Asia, that's a very low intensity market because the productivity needs are very different apart from very specialized customers. Standard would be next, and premium is a very small part of the market. So hopefully, that gives you a sense of, both by geography and application, how these are really targeted. In terms of our own growth, we're seeing high growth in both the lower intensity and the standard product line while maintaining our customers from -- for the premium truck.

These free Google alternatives make it easy to break up with the tech giant.

On Tuesday, Nov. 3, Google announced that starting next year AI tools will be turned off by default in software used by K-12 students. Teachers and administrators will have to enable the features for students to use them in Google Search.

“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, said, according to the New York Times. He also said if a school bans Google’s AI tools, students “will not have access to Search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

If you’re a parent or educator, you should know you don’t have to use Google Search to teach your children. There are plenty of other free search engines you can try now.

It’s also important to note that using these search engines in Google Chrome may prevent you from getting their full benefits. Here are five free alternatives to Google Search.

Brave also offers other features, like a VPN, a crypto wallet and its own AI assistant named Leo. And Brave said your AI usage is private and secure as well. You don’t even need to create or log into an account to use Leo.

This private, Berlin-based search engine is also a green option. Ecosia writes online it has planted over 250 million trees and produces more clean energy than it takes to power all its searches and AI queries. The company also writes online that all its profits go toward climate action.

This French-based search engine writes online it doesn’t retain your search data or sell your personal data, making it a good alternative to Google. In addition to search, Qwant also offers a feature called Qwant Junior, which it writes online is meant to help children between the ages of 6 and 12 years old safely explore the internet.

You should know that Qwant has integrated AI into its engine in what it calls Flash Answers. But you can deactivate it from your Settings menu without jumping through hoops. Historically, Qwant has used Bing’s search API, which lets companies access Bing’s search infrastructure. But according to CNBC, the company partnered with Berlin-based search engine Ecosia in 2024 to build a European search index in order to reduce dependence on US companies.

Startpage is a search engine that’s also a search aggregator. That means it partners with other companies like Google and Microsoft Bing to bring you search results.

For more on other search engines, here’s what to know about DuckDuckGo and Brave Search.

Netflix is adding a new Discover feature, which recommends tailored streaming selections. Here's how it works.

AI tools are all over the internet, in the workplace, in your apps — and now there’s one coming on Netflix. The streaming giant just announced a new AI feature for the TV app called AI Discover, which will help users find titles that match their moods and interests. It’s initially being rolled out to a small group of users in the US whose language is set to English. To find out if you have access, check your Netflix navigation bar for the word “Discover” with a red gem icon next to it and a “New” label.

Also: Roku is taking away a fan-favorite screensaver

The AI Discover tab will be centered around themes. You’ll be able to pick from a range of themes depending on what you feel like watching, or how long you want to watch. You’ll also see selections that match what you’ve been watching lately and what’s popular.

You can refresh the list of suggestions or dive deeper with more complex search prompts. If you’d like to start over, you can pick the “Something different” option. To support AI Discover, Netflix is also adding a new button next to Play and My List that’ll let you tune your recommendations. You can press this button to keep a recommendation or to request that you don’t be recommended a title again.

Most streaming apps already rely quite heavily on machine learning and AI algorithms to offer user recommendations, even if they’re not marketed as AI features. Though most rely on traditional AI algorithms, like Prime Video’s “Recommended for you” tab, they personalize title recommendations based on your viewing history, likes and dislikes, and rental behavior.

Other platforms offer generative AI and features more similar to Netflix’s AI Discover. For example, YouTube features Gemini-powered searches that let you ask complex questions or use open-ended prompts to get results you want.

Also: The best early Black Friday TV deals are all at Best Buy

Some smart TV interfaces — including including Roku, Fire TV, Google TV, and, coming soon, Apple TV — have also adopted generative AI in their operating systems to let you use voice search with more naturally worded requests, and the system generates cross-platform results.

While I am itching to test this feature to see just how accurate it can be, Netflix hasn’t made it widely available yet. The company will gradually grant users access over the coming weeks, so stay tuned.

#3247. If the White House Network Can Be Hijacked by Proxies, Your Smart Home Is Already at Risk

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

A new report finds residential proxies exiting the White House network 236 times in the past month.

As if the Trump administration needed any more bad news this week, cybersecurity researchers discovered several residential proxy services originating from the White House network, exposing a potential security flaw that could allow cybercriminals to route traffic through official government IP addresses.

The security firm Layer3 Intel detected residential proxy activity on AS2650, a network registered to the Executive Office of the President. Another security firm identified software from the proxy server Infatica, a company owned by a Russian entrepreneur who ran a server-rental company used by hackers in attacks on election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

While there’s no evidence that proxy access was used to carry out attacks on the White House, experts say it could open the door for hackers to exploit vulnerabilities or grant outsiders an unmonitored back door into high-security systems.

“It basically gives them a foothold on a network where previously nobody was getting into the White House network,” Layer3 founder Sergiy Usatyuk told CNET. “From a security policy perspective, it gives you all types of potential pathways to exploit.” (Usatyuk pleaded guilty to federal charges in 2019 for his role in operating websites that launched denial-of-service, or DDoS, attacks.)

Residential proxy services route internet traffic through consumer devices (such as smartphones, laptops or home routers) to make it appear that the activity is being performed by a real person. While proxies can be used for relatively benign purposes — web scraping is by far the most common use case — they’re also popular for activities like malware attacks, identity theft and creating fake social media accounts.

For example, earlier this year, Synthient, another company that tracks proxies and VPNs, documented how one botnet infected more than 2 million devices using a residential proxy server. If a similar vulnerability existed in the White House proxy, hackers could probe the infected device’s internal systems and install malicious payloads.

In its report, Layer3 found traffic from six distinct IP addresses exiting the White House network from at least 28 known residential proxy services between Oct. 5 and Nov. 3, with most activity occurring in the evenings between 5 p.m. and midnight EST. This suggests the culprit may be an employee who connected a personal device to a Wi-Fi network with a compromised app or a proxy SDK (software development kit) running in the background. Third-party SDKs can convert a device into a “proxy node.”

Commercial proxy networks sell access to these nodes, so anyone with a few dollars could rent a trusted IP address — in this case, making it appear as though traffic originates from the Executive Office of the President.

Researchers at Synthient provided more details about the case, posting on X that several White House staffers are running “a Windows 11 machine with InfaticaSDK installed.” They pointed directly to Rave, a popular app that lets users watch streaming services with friends, as the likely delivery mechanism for the residential proxy traffic detected on the White House network.

Riley Kilmer, co-founder of the cybersecurity firm Spur Intelligence, wrote in a LinkedIn post that different types of proxy companies had been discovered in the White House, including one called 9Proxy, which is often used by criminals for banking fraud.

The White House didn’t respond to CNET’s request for comment.

Because smart TVs, connected appliances and home routers usually have minimal user oversight, a single unvetted app or out-of-date firmware update can turn a household of IoT devices into an exit node for commercial proxy networks.

Proxies can generally “glom” onto consumer devices by embedding networking code directly into software, either consensually (users willingly install it) or nonconsensually (by exploiting unsecured device access points).

It starts when app developers look for revenue by integrating those proxy SDKs into their free apps. Then, when you install the app, the fine print of the terms and conditions of service often includes a clause that allows the app to add your IP address to a third-party proxy pool.

A June report from Spur Intelligence found that roughly one in three apps available on Samsung and LG smart TVs were selling users’ IP addresses. To avoid ads, users often accept the terms when downloading the app — a type of unnoticed consent. Once installed, the SDK runs continuously in the background, registering the device’s IP with the proxy provider’s gateway, unless you delete the app or opt out. (The report notes that Amazon and Roku have explicitly banned this practice.)

Using a free VPN could expose you to the same risk, allowing your IP address to be used by someone else for nefarious activities. The FBI’s guidance on protecting yourself against proxies specifically calls out free VPNs as one of the primary ways bad actors gain access to an IP address.

In some cases, you don’t need to download anything to get your IP thrown into a shady proxy pool — you just have to buy the wrong device. A recent investigation by Synthient discovered that more than 1.3 million streaming devices from the China-based device manufacturer MECOOL were infected with proxy SDKs. A proxy service called SocksEscort was charged by the Justice Department in March with compromising thousands of routers to submit fraudulent unemployment insurance claims.

Checking whether your IP address is being used by a proxy service without your knowledge is relatively simple. Layer3 provides a free proxy-checking tool that searches its database of over 70 million proxies to find if yours is listed. GreyNoise, another cybersecurity company, also offers a free IP-checking service.

These tools can tell you if proxy traffic is passing through your network, but they can’t identify which specific device has the SDK running. You’ll have to do some additional detective work to figure out the culprit. Some common sources include free VPNs, gaming apps, “one price, no subscriptions” streaming boxes and smart TVs.

Cybersecurity experts also recommend keeping the firmware on all your internet-connected devices up to date and downloading only from trusted app stores.

New developer beta release notes point to deeper Siri AI integration and more Safari customization.

Developer betas for MacOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and iOS 27.3 are here, with a few major upgrades to the Safari browser. Vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, and deeper Siri AI integration are on the way to the public, but are first in beta for testing.

Siri AI is expected to be further woven into Music, Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Safari. Adaptive dark mode will allow for any website to be viewed in dark mode, even if the site doesn’t support it. Finally, vertical tabs are pretty straightforward, enabling vertical navigation and drag-and-drop tab reorganization.

Here’s what you can expect when the software goes public in mid-December.

Also: 3 handy iPhone features that make my life easier – even doing laundry

Siri AI gains more access to your Apple devices, allowing more cross-app functionality and the ability to execute complex, multi-step tasks within your apps.

According to 9to5Mac, you can ask Siri AI to create a playlist in Music and save it to your library, request messages to be scheduled for a later send, organize and label photos, and create a detailed calendar invite — all with your voice.

The same reporting also states that Siri AI features will appear in Maps, Weather, Shortcuts, and Notes, signaling that an AI-supercharged Siri will live in every crevice of your Apple devices.

Also: iOS 27 will organize your open Safari tabs now

I’m not one to complete tasks like the ones mentioned above on my iPhone — I’m far more likely to do them on my MacBook Air, since I associate the laptop with productivity. Every blue moon I’ll rearrange my entire Apple Music catalog, every month I fill out my calendar, and sometimes I’ll go through Photos and try to organize it. I can see myself automating certain steps in these tasks, and I’m excited to try it.

A WebKit blog post details that adaptive dark mode is coming to Safari, how it will work, and what users can expect. According to the post, 40% of web page loads are from dark mode users, but only 10% of web pages natively support it.

I’m particularly excited about this feature, as I set my Apple devices to automatically enable dark mode at 7 p.m. to encourage a more relaxing evening scrolling vibe, especially while reading. I read a lot on my MacBook, and in a dark room, a bright page can feel too bright, but dimming my laptop’s display doesn’t quite do the trick.

Also: Your AirPods got better in iOS 27 – three new ways I’m using them

The WebKit blog post states that adaptive dark mode uses “a color matrix to invert the luminosity of colors while preserving hue” and distinguishes between when a page’s color is purely decorative and when it carries substantial meaning, to ensure the user experience remains consistent between light and dark modes.

Vertical browser tabs aren’t a new concept, but they’ll soon be new to Safari. I see the value in vertical tabs: a list view is easier to scan, web page titles aren’t smushed when several tabs are open, and they’re particularly useful when you’re working on a widescreen monitor.

Many people who spend hours using their Mac or MacBook may find this upcoming feature useful. I do believe that Safari is the superior browser for personal use, given its integration with your Apple devices, especially with features like Handoff.

Also: 7 AI-free iOS 27 features that make old iPhones exciting again

However, I do have one major gripe with vertical tabs: they’re usually locked to the left panel, and I prefer the right. If Safari allows this customization, I’ll seriously consider switching from horizontal tabs.

#3243. Want an AI job? Deployment engineers are earning executive-level pay – up to $1.45M a year

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

AI has ushered in new jobs, and some of them are paying handsomely, according to a new study.

AI engineers are making well over six figures in salary — and plenty more in bonuses and equity, according to data from a new report by executive search firm Christian & Timbers.

Enterprises now pay “elite” AI deployment engineers between $586,000 and $1.45 million annually in total compensation, with senior leaders in the field earning up to $2.25 million, according to the report. This figure approaches the median compensation of executive officers of public companies, the authors note.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

Christian & Timbers is an AI executive search and leadership advisory firm, recruiting CEOs, board members, technology executives, and AI engineers for enterprises. The new report draws on more than 550 interviews with engineers, deployment leaders, and executives conducted from January through June 2026, along with closed and current open offers. The compensation bands are Christian & Timbers’ estimates and represent ranges rather than statistical averages.

“Enterprise CEOs are under pressure to deliver returns for their AI investments. The most important decision is how to build the team that delivers on that goal,” said Jeff Christian, founder and CEO of Christian & Timbers, in a press release.

Also: What workers are really using AI for in 2026 – and what they aren’t

The report noted that the staggering salary range includes base salary, bonus, and annualized equity. Christian & Timbers said it defines an “elite” forward deployment engineer (FDE) as “a senior AI-native deployment builder, typically with 7 to 15 years of experience, including at least two years building and deploying agentic automated workflows that deliver measurable ROI with a documented enterprise impact of $10M or more,” who has also led a team of other forward deployment engineers.

Also: 50% of companies generate value from AI now – here’s how

The large salary ranges reflect increasing enterprise investments in AI talent and employee development. Microsoft, AWS, and OpenAI have announced more than $7.5 billion in corporate and partner investment in AI deployment over the past six months, Christian & Timbers noted in the release.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

There’s an increasing need to fill roles such as Senior Principal AI Engineer, AI Solutions Engineer, and Head of Deployment — but there is a limited pool of qualified candidates. The firm estimates that only 2,000 of the most senior deployment leaders exist in the US market, according to a previous Christian & Timbers study, which does not meet demand — so companies are competing for the same small group of professionals, hence the increasing salaries.

While the report underscores lucrative yields for certain engineering roles, the firm said that public job titles make comparisons more challenging.

“Christian & Timbers’ elite category spans several titles, while advertised FDE roles cover a broader range of experience and responsibilities. Experienced deployment engineers may be recruited directly or promoted into the work under titles such as staff software engineer or principal AI engineer,” the study said.

Plus, equity and bonus make up 52% to 66% of senior engineer pay, and most job postings don’t include that value in the salary, the report noted.
